stories.summary: A long-standing land dispute turned fatal in Bhadohi district of Uttar Pradesh on Tuesday morning, with a young man being shot dead during a violent altercation, police said. The incident occurred around 10 a.m. in Jangla Banpurwa village, under the Ghosia outpost of Aurai police station. According to the police, two brothers were erecting barriers on their agricultural land when a neighbouring landowner, accompanied by seven to eight men, arrived at the spot and objected, leading to a confrontation. The dispute soon escalated into violence, with both sides allegedly using sticks and clubs. During the clash, one of the assailants reportedly opened fire with a revolver, killing one of the brothers on the spot. His sibling sustained a gunshot injury to his hand. Two others were also injured in the incident. Tension prevailed in the village when the police moved the body for post-mortem examination, as the deceased’s parents lay down in front of the ambulance in protest. Senior officials intervened and persuaded the family members to allow the procedure to continue. The deceased’s wife, who is eight months pregnant, reportedly lost consciousness after learning of the incident and is undergoing treatment. Police officials said the land dispute between the two parties had been continuing for nearly seven years. A case has been registered, and efforts are on to identify and arrest the accused. Further investigation is underway. First see the pictures of the crime scene... Dispute escalates into violence Police officials said the situation escalated after a neighbouring landowner arrived at the site with seven to eight men and objected to the construction. What began as a verbal altercation soon turned violent, with both sides allegedly attacking each other using sticks and batons. During the clash, one of the assailants allegedly opened fire with a revolver, killing Ashish Yadav (26) on the spot. His brother, Akhilesh Yadav, sustained a bullet injury to his left hand, while their uncle Rajnath Yadav suffered serious injuries after being assaulted with sticks. Two others were also injured in the incident. Ashish Yadav was rushed to the Aurai Community Health Centre but was declared dead on arrival. Rajnath Yadav was later referred to Banaras Hindu University Hospital in Varanasi for further treatment, while Akhilesh Yadav was treated and discharged. Seven-year-old dispute over four biswa land Police said the clash stemmed from a long-standing dispute over four biswa of agricultural land. According to the victim’s family, the dispute has been continuing since 2009 between Ashish Yadav and Dr. Brijesh Kumar Yadav, with a court stay currently in force on the land. Ashish’s uncle, Umashankar Yadav, told the police that the land was ancestral property and alleged that the opposing side had been pressuring the family to part with it. A related case has been pending in court for the past four years, he said. According to the complaint, Dr. Brijesh Kumar Yadav arrived at the disputed site along with his son Anoop Yadav, brother Girjesh Yadav, nephew Sachin Yadav and several others. During the scuffle, Anoop Yadav allegedly pulled out his licensed revolver and fired three rounds, one of which fatally hit Ashish Yadav in the abdomen. Protest over post-mortem Tension gripped the village when the police attempted to take the body for post-mortem examination. The deceased’s parents, Phoolchand and Isravati, lay down in front of the ambulance, demanding the immediate arrest of all those involved. Senior police officials, including the Circle Officer, reached the spot and assured the family that action was being taken. After being shown photographs of the accused who had been detained, the family agreed to allow the post-mortem to proceed. Family in grief Scenes of grief prevailed at Ashish Yadav’s home, where family members were seen breaking down repeatedly. His wife, who is eight months pregnant, reportedly fainted several times after learning of his death and is undergoing treatment. The couple also has a two-year-old daughter. Officials from the women’s police station visited the family and assured them of strict action against those responsible. Police action and investigation Superintendent of Police Abhimanyu Manglik said three accused had been taken into custody and efforts were on to arrest another suspect. “One person has died and three others have been injured in a violent clash over a land dispute. Statements of family members are being recorded, and appropriate legal action will be taken against those responsible,” he said. A heavy police force has been deployed in the village to prevent any further unrest. The Sub-Divisional Magistrate of Aurai and other revenue officials also visited the village, met the bereaved family and assured them of administrative support and an impartial investigation.

stories.title: Vishwa Hindu Parishad convoy leaves Gonda for Murshidabad:Police stop procession in Lucknow; VHP president put under house arrest
stories.summary: Workers of the Vishwa Hindu Parishad from several districts of Uttar Pradesh, including Lucknow and Gonda, attempted to leave for Murshidabad on Tuesday amid heightened tensions over a controversial religious structure. While a group from Gonda departed in 10 vehicles under the leadership of Social Justice Cell state president Arya Heeru, police in Lucknow stopped another convoy of 15 vehicles, leading to a two-hour protest by workers carrying saffron flags, axes and spades. VHP state president Gopal Rai was placed under house arrest as a preventive measure. The mobilisation follows claims that West Bengal MLA Humayun Kabir is overseeing the construction of a Babri Masjid in Murshidabad, where nearly two lakh people reportedly gathered with bricks during a foundation ceremony. Hindu organisations have objected to the move, with VHP leaders publicly declaring plans to travel from Uttar Pradesh to Murshidabad to stop and demolish the structure—announcements that were also displayed on hoardings across several cities, including Lucknow. First look at these 3 pictures... Workers arrived with saffron flags and spades Officials of Vishwa Hindu Raksha Parishad said that workers are marching from most districts including Gonda, Bahraich, Barabanki and Lucknow. About 15,000 members and officials from UP, Madhya Pradesh and Delhi are going to West Bengal Murshidabad. Said that they will not allow even a single brick to be laid in the name of Babri anywhere in India including West Bengal. All people are carrying saffron flags, spades and axes. Posters with anti-West Bengal government slogans are pasted on vehicles. State President Prakash Arya Heeru said that they have set out on the call of their national leadership in protest against the alleged announcement made by the MLA of Murshidabad regarding mosque construction. If a mosque is built there, it should be named after former President APJ Abdul Kalam or martyr Veer Abdul Hamid. Hoardings were put up on February 8 On February 8, Vishwa Hindu Raksha Parishad put up 5 hoardings between 1090 intersection and Gomti Nagar. They mentioned the under-construction Babri Masjid in Murshidabad. On one side were pictures of Lord Ram and Vishwa Hindu Raksha Parishad president Gopal Rai. Now read about the Murshidabad Babri Mosque controversy... In Beldanga of Murshidabad district in West Bengal, TMC suspended MLA Humayun Kabir laid the foundation stone of a mosque on December 6, which was to be built in the style of Ayodhya's Babri Masjid. During this, slogans of Nara-e-Takbir, Allahu Akbar were raised. More than 2 lakh people gathered at the event. On November 25, Humayun Kabir had said that he would lay the foundation stone of Babri Masjid on December 6, marking 33 years of the demolition of the disputed structure in Ayodhya. TMC suspended Humayun Kabir from the party on December 4. Humayun had said - if 100 Muslims become martyrs, they will take 500 with them Speaking to the media about building the Babri Masjid in Murshidabad on November 28, 2025, Humayun Kabir gave another controversial statement. He said, 'Whoever tries to stop them will face serious consequences. If 100 Muslims become martyrs, they will take 500 people with them.' Humayun Kabir has previously been in discussions for controversial statements. During the 2024 Lok Sabha election campaign in Shaktipur, Murshidabad, Humayun Kabir said in a public meeting, 'I will quit politics if I don't drown you (Hindus) in the Bhagirathi river within two hours. You are 30%, we are 70% (Muslims). I won't let you live in Shaktipur.' After this statement, the Election Commission had issued him a notice. Meanwhile, TMC had distanced itself from this statement. Mosque dispute is one year old The entire dispute started in November 2024. At that time, TMC MLA Humayun Kabir had talked about making a small replica of the Babri Masjid of Ayodhya. When controversy arose over the use of the name Babri, he had said that Babri Masjid is an emotional issue for Muslims. After this, in December 2024 itself, BJP talked about building Ram Temple in Murshidabad. However, even then BJP leader Shankar Ghosh had said that Ram Temple should not be seen as a response to the mosque. Temple is part of culture, while Babri Masjid has a bad history, how can it be built in Bengal.

stories.title: ‘Those who ordered firing are now building Ram Mandir':Akhilesh’s barb triggers clash with BJP MPs; Parliament witnesses sharp exchanges
stories.summary: Akhilesh Yadav launched a sharp attack on the Union government and the Uttar Pradesh administration during the Budget discussion in the Lok Sabha on Tuesday, alleging that the Budget was “directionless” and offered nothing to the poor, farmers and workers. Speaking amid repeated interventions from Treasury benches, the Samajwadi Party president said that the government had replaced the language of self-reliance and swadeshi with what he termed unilateral trade concessions, particularly in relation to the United States. “Concessions, not a deal with America” Mr. Yadav questioned claims that a trade “deal” had been finalised with the U.S., arguing that India had opened its markets without reciprocal benefits. “It is not a deal with America, it is a compromise,” he said, asking why, if such an agreement was imminent, it had taken 11 months to materialise. Referring to tariff figures, he posed a jibe to the government: “The country wants to know whether zero is bigger or 18.” He alleged that inflation had surged while ordinary citizens received no tax relief, and that social security measures remained “only on paper”. Farmers and labourers, he said, were “searching the Budget with binoculars” to find any benefit meant for them. Poetry and protest in the House Lacing his speech with poetry, Mr. Yadav cited Mirza Ghalib to underline what he called the gap between official claims and lived reality. He also mocked what he described as the government’s habit of building “castles in the air” while ignoring practical concerns. Responding to heckling from ruling party MPs, he said governments could intimidate many, but “cannot scare those who refuse to bow”. In a cultural aside, he remarked that if some could not manage a namaste, they were welcome in Lucknow to offer an adaab. Ram temple remark sparks exchange The SP leader also drew attention to changes in nomenclature under the rural employment scheme, saying the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act had been renamed “VBG Ramji”, while actor Arun Govil, who portrayed Ram on television and is now an MP, was seated at the back benches. As ruling party members countered him by invoking the 1990 firing on kar sevaks, Mr. Yadav retorted that “those who ordered the firing are now building the Ram temple”. He was widely seen as alluding to Nripendra Mishra, who currently chairs the Ram Temple Construction Committee and served as principal secretary to Mulayam Singh Yadav in 1990. Mr. Mishra has earlier maintained that he had opposed the use of force at the disputed site. Kashi heritage, reservations and law-and-order Mr. Yadav accused the government of damaging the heritage of Kashi, alleging that a statue of Rajmata Ahilyabai Holkar at Manikarnika Ghat had been demolished and that several temples had been removed. He also claimed that a historic bell gifted by the King of Nepal had gone missing. Raising concerns over reservations, he said India could be considered truly developed only when Dalits, backward classes and Muslims enjoyed equal rights. He cited the case of 72-year-old Moeed Khan, who he said was jailed for 19 months in Ayodhya despite being innocent, as evidence of political misuse of the law. “Eleven Budgets, incomes not rising” Criticising the government’s economic record, Mr. Yadav said per capita income had not risen despite 11 Budgets, and that promises such as doubling farmers’ income and generating employment had remained unfulfilled. He warned that indiscriminate imports would leave farmers with no viable crops to grow. “A good Budget has three markers — progress of the poor, prosperity and smiles,” he said. “This Budget has taken away all three.” He also cautioned against China’s growing economic influence, urging the government to act with vigilance, and said the Finance Minister should clarify the government’s position on MGNREGA in the House. The Treasury benches did not immediately respond to the allegations.

stories.title: 'Babri Masjid will never be rebuilt, Doomsday will never come':Yogi Adityanath draws a final line on Babri, issues stern law-and-order warning
stories.summary: Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath on Tuesday said that the reconstruction of the Babri Masjid was “never possible”, asserting that the “night of Doomsday will never come” and warning that those who violated the law would face severe consequences. He urged people to “learn to live within the law in India”, stating that defiance of the law would lead to punishment. Addressing a public gathering in Barabanki, the Chief Minister described the BJP-led dispensation as a “double-engine government” and reiterated the party’s long-standing position on the Ram temple in Ayodhya. “We had said earlier — Ram Lalla, we will come and build the temple at the same place. The temple has been built. Is there any doubt?” he said. Mr. Adityanath further remarked that those who “forget Lord Ram” would not succeed, asserting that there was “no place” for those opposed to Ram or for those who had attacked Ram devotees, while adding that Ram belonged to everyone without discrimination. Ram has forgotten them, there is no place for them Referring to temple development, the Chief Minister said work on the Loshweshwar temple was progressing rapidly and would continue. He said the present government fulfilled the promises it made. Speaking about the Ram temple in Ayodhya, he said the government had delivered on its commitment to build the temple. He added that there should be no doubt about the government’s resolve. He said those who opposed Lord Ram had no place today. He added that Lord Ram belonged to all and that there was no discrimination, but some people ignored him for political reasons. He urged people to follow the law and live responsibly in the country. No one was safe before 2017 Mr. Adityanath said that before 2017, law and order had deteriorated and land belonging to the poor was encroached upon. He claimed that the situation improved after his government assumed office. He said women, traders and ordinary citizens now felt safer. He added that salaries were being paid on time and pensions were reaching beneficiaries. According to him, the State was witnessing steady development. He said the government followed a zero-tolerance policy and warned that those who took the law into their hands would face strict action. When Modi came, the poor got houses The Chief Minister said that large-scale housing for the poor became possible after Narendra Modi became Prime Minister. He said around 60 lakh people in Uttar Pradesh had received houses under the Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana. He said villages earlier lacked electricity, sanitation facilities and proper roads. He claimed that electricity had now reached all 75 districts, toilets had been built in homes and clean drinking water was being provided. Temple not built in 500 years Mr. Adityanath said that despite several rulers and governments over the last 500 years, including after Independence, no effort was made to build the Ram temple in Ayodhya. He said the temple was built during the BJP-led government and that lakhs of devotees were now visiting Ayodhya for darshan. He also said that sanitation facilities had expanded, ensuring toilets in homes and reducing hardships faced by women. He added that the government was supporting girls from birth to marriage, calling it a shared responsibility of society.

stories.title: UGC regulation march turns tense in Lucknow:Police allegedly pull Pallavi Patel by hair during detention near Assembly route
stories.summary: Tension flared in Uttar Pradesh’s capital on Tuesday as a confrontation broke out between the police and Pallavi Patel during a protest march in support of the UGC Equity Regulation 2026. Pallavi Patel, president of Apna Dal (Kamerawadi) and an ally of the Samajwadi Party, was leading a foot march along with hundreds of supporters, including a large number of women. The march began from IT Chauraha and was headed towards the Vidhan Sabha. Police stop march near reserve police lines As the procession approached the Reserve Police Lines, police personnel stopped the march using heavy barbed barricades. When Pallavi Patel attempted to climb over the barricades, police intervened, leading to a scuffle between her and the security personnel. Following the confrontation, Pallavi sat down on the road in protest, staging a sit-in at the spot. Protesters detained after failed negotiations Police officials tried for nearly 15 minutes to persuade Pallavi to disperse, but she refused to move. Subsequently, the police began detaining protesters one by one and placing them into police vehicles. While most of the supporters were taken into custody, Pallavi lay down on the road, forcing police to struggle to move her towards the vehicle. Allegations of force during detention According to eyewitness accounts, Pallavi reached the police vehicle but resisted entering it. A woman police officer attempted to guide her inside by holding her arms and back, but when she continued to resist, the officer allegedly pulled her by the hair and pushed her into the vehicle. Pallavi Patel’s stand on UGC regulations Pallavi Patel later said that delaying the implementation of the UGC Equity Regulation 2026 amounted to a direct injustice against the rights of reserved and marginalized communities. Pallavi Patel is currently the MLA from the Sirathu assembly constituency in Kaushambi district and heads Apna Dal (Kamerawadi), which is presently in alliance with the Samajwadi Party.

stories.title: UP Budget Session:Speaker orders seizure of MLAs’ phones after disruption in House; Dy CM Keshav issues stern warning on reservation irregularities
stories.summary: On the second day of the Uttar Pradesh Legislature’s Budget Session, Speaker Satish Mahana lost his temper with two MLAs after their mobile phones rang during the tribute to deceased legislators. The Speaker immediately summoned security personnel. Pointing towards the two members, he instructed security to take their phones, saying, “Take the telephones from both the honourable members… the ones sitting at the back wearing caps.” It is learnt that the phones belonged to BJP Fatehpur Sikri MLA Chaudhary Babulal and another legislator. On the second day of the session, the House paid tributes to the departed MLAs. Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, who was present in the Assembly, remembered the deceased legislators and recalled their contributions. Leader of the Opposition Mata Prasad Pandey also paid tributes, followed by floor leaders of all parties. After the tribute proceedings, members observed two minutes of silence. The Assembly was then adjourned till Wednesday. The House functioned for about 35 minutes on the second day. On February 11, Finance Minister Suresh Khanna will present the final Budget of the Yogi government’s second term. Reservation issue raised in Legislative Council, SP MLCs stage protest In the Legislative Council, Samajwadi Party MLCs, including Man Singh Yadav and Lal Bihari Yadav, raised the issue of alleged irregularities in reservation across various recruitment processes. When Deputy Chief Minister Keshav Prasad Maurya responded, the Opposition termed his reply inadequate and staged a sit-in inside the House. SP MLCs sat on the floor and raised slogans, forcing the Chair to adjourn the Council for 15 minutes. During the tribute proceedings, the ringing of two MLAs’ mobile phones prompted the Speaker to call security and order the immediate seizure of the devices. The Assembly paid tributes to MLAs Shyam Bihari Lal and Vijay Singh Gaur. Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath highlighted their achievements and contributions. The Assembly has been adjourned till Wednesday. The Budget will be presented on February 11.

stories.summary: A bride in Uttar Pradesh’s Kaushambi district died by suicide after allegedly being harassed and threatened by her former lover, just hours before her wedding. The woman consumed poison at her home late Sunday night and was rushed to the hospital, where doctors declared her dead. According to police, the woman was set to marry a police officer on Monday, February 10. For several days before the wedding, her former lover had been sending messages and making threatening calls to the groom on WhatsApp. He claimed he had been in a relationship with the bride for six years and repeatedly asked the groom not to marry her. When the groom asked for proof, the man said he would show it and again pleaded with him to stop the marriage. The groom later scolded the man and filed a complaint at the police station. After this, a heated argument reportedly took place between the bride and her former lover. Police said wedding preparations were underway at both homes when, around 12.30 am, the bride consumed poison. She was taken to SRN Hospital in Prayagraj, where she died during treatment. stories.title: National volleyball player found dead in hostel:Undergoing training at a sports academy in Prayagraj, returned from a wedding 2 days ago
stories.summary: The body of a national-level volleyball player was found lying inside a hostel room in Prayagraj. He was training at the Amitabh Bachchan Sports Complex. On Tuesday morning around 6 am, junior players went to call him, but the room door did not open. When they looked inside, Pratyush was found lying unconscious. After receiving the information, coach Veer Singh and others took Pratyush to Bailey Hospital, where doctors declared him dead. Pratyush’s uncle, Dr Santosh, said they were informed that the hostel room door was not locked from inside. The coach also said that children usually do not lock their doors in the hostel. Pratyush Rai was originally from Sauri village in Ghazipur district. He had been living at the Myohal Sports Complex for the past four years and was training in volleyball. He had played at the national level twice for the Uttar Pradesh team. His hostel room partner, Rishabh, had gone to his village for the past few days. Pratyush’s father, Avni Kumar Rai, is a farmer, while his mother, Reena Rai, is a homemaker. The family was informed about his death at around 6.30 am, after which they left for Prayagraj. Pratyush’s uncle, Dr Santosh, also reached the post-mortem house directly from Varanasi. On seeing her son’s body, the mother collapsed. The entire family was inconsolable. Uncle says three versions heard at the hostel Dr Santosh said that when they reached the hostel, different people gave different accounts. Some said Pratyush’s body was found on the floor, others said it was on the bed, while some claimed it was near the door. He said the family does not want to say anything at this stage and is waiting for the post-mortem report. Selected for Junior Asia Cup Pratyush had been selected for the Junior Asia Cup, which was scheduled to be held in June-July. He had recently returned after playing the Junior Nationals in Rajasthan. In December, his team won the state-level Mahant Avaidyanath Prize Money Tournament held in Gorakhpur, where Pratyush was also named the best player. Youngest among four siblings Pratyush was the youngest among four siblings. He had gone to Ghazipur on 5 February to attend his cousin’s wedding and returned to Prayagraj on 7 February. His brother-in-law works as a revenue official in Prayagraj. Karnalganj Police Station in-charge Sanjay Singh said- The cause of death will only be clear after the post-mortem report comes. The matter is being investigated from every angle.

stories.title: Allahabad High Court stays FIR against ASP Anuj Chaudhary:Orders relief after lower court's directive in Sambhal violence case
stories.summary: In the Sambhal violence case, the Allahabad High Court has granted major relief to Additional Superintendent of Police Anuj Chaudhary by temporarily staying the Sambhal CJM court’s order directing registration of an FIR against police personnel. The High Court heard petitions filed by the Uttar Pradesh government and ASP Anuj Chaudhary on Monday, challenging the lower court’s order on multiple grounds. The matter was also taken up on Tuesday, during which all parties presented their arguments. After the hearing, the High Court granted interim relief to ASP Anuj Chaudhary and fixed the next hearing after five weeks. Hearing lasted for two hours yesterday In the high-profile case related to Sambhal violence, the hearing lasted for two hours on February 9. During this, the UP government presented its side in the matter. Arguments were presented between both parties. Why FIR orders were issued against police personnel? SP Krishna Kumar Bishnoi had said - A judicial inquiry into the violence has already been conducted. Therefore, this FIR will not be registered. We will appeal against the court's decision. 4 people died in violence during the survey on November 24, 2024 Judge who ordered FIR against ASP Anuj was removed The Allahabad High Court had transferred 14 judges on the evening of January 20. The list also included three district judge level officers. The surprising name on the list was Vibhanshu Sudhir, the Chief Judicial Magistrate (CJM) of Sambhal. Vibhanshu had ordered the registration of an FIR against 20 policemen, including ASP Anuj Chaudhary, on January 9. Vibhanshu has been transferred and sent to Sultanpur as Civil Judge Senior Division. Aditya Singh, Civil Judge Senior Division of Chandausi, has been entrusted with the responsibility of the new CJM of Sambhal. Aditya Singh himself had ordered a survey on the claim of Shri Harihar Mandir vs. Shahi Jama Masjid in Sambhal. Aditya Kumar Singh has been promoted.

stories.title: Am I a terrorist? asks 'The Manipur Diary' film director:Magh Mela administration denies permission to Sanoj Mishra for trailer launch
stories.summary: Viral girl Monalisa will launch the trailer of her film 'The Diary of Manipur' today at the Prayagraj Magh Mela during Mahakumbh. However, the Magh Mela administration has not given permission for the film's trailer launch. The administration said - According to the police department's report, considering the excessive crowd and security concerns, you cannot get permission. After February 15, when the crowd is less, then you will get permission. Film Director Sanoj Mishra said - No problem, I don't want it. I will talk to CM sir tomorrow. What report has come against me? Am I a terrorist? I am working for the country. I am working for Sanatan Dharma. This is very wrong. Monalisa released a video, said - Coming to Prayagraj on February 10 Monalisa, who came into discussion during Mahakumbh, released her video a day before, saying - Today, I am coming to Prayagraj. The launch of the film's trailer is no less than a dream for me. She said - A year ago, with the blessings of Mother Ganga and all of you, I have come this far. Please continue to give your love and blessings. Film Director said - I am working for Sanatan 'The Diary of Manipur' film director Sanoj Mishra said - At the campus I have chosen, you won't find more than 2 people. Only media people will come. Not more than 50 people will come. I am coming because I started from here a year ago. I have trained a Banjara girl and brought her into the film. If I get permission after February 15, I will do the program in Dubai. Everything here has been uprooted. Even the tent has been uprooted. Many devotees have left. Unfortunately, I didn't get permission. My team's tickets are already booked. I don't know who is causing this. This is wrong for me and wrong for my team. Now know how Monalisa became famous in Mahakumbh... Monalisa is from Madhya Pradesh Monalisa is from Maheshwar in Khargone district of Madhya Pradesh. Monalisa and her family had gone to sell garlands at the Prayagraj Mahakumbh. She quickly went viral on social media for her eyes and simplicity. Since then, her videos have been getting a lot of views. She became so famous that T-shirts with her picture started selling. Later, she wrote on social media that she was troubled by media people and many others. Her health had also deteriorated. Monalisa said - I was feeling good there, but I was not able to sell garlands. People would surround me. Troubled by this, I left Mahakumbh and returned home. Now read about Sanoj Mishra, who gave Monalisa her break Sanoj Mishra said - 'I was already working on The Diary of Manipur'. During that time, the Mahakumbh was organized in Prayagraj. That's where I learned about Monalisa and heard the story of her struggles. The crowd was so large that people were only busy taking selfies and making videos there. Because of this, all their work and business came to a halt. They lost their livelihood, and various rumors and fears emerged. Things got to the point where there was talk of kidnapping. After this, I offered Monalisa the film.

stories.title: 5 members of a family found dead in Mathura:Couple and three children, suicide notes recovered from 3 places, 2 theories on deaths
stories.summary: Dead bodies of a husband, his wife and their three children were found in Mathura. Initial reports suggest that the entire family may have consumed poison mixed in milk, pointing towards a possible suicide. However, police are also probing the case from a murder angle. The incident came to light on Monday morning when none of the family members woke up until late. Growing suspicious, neighbours alerted the police. A police team reached the spot and began collecting evidence from the house. According to police officials, statements of family members and villagers are being recorded. The exact cause of death will be confirmed only after the post-mortem reports are received. The incident occurred in Khapparpur village under the Mahavan police station area. Jaikishan is Manish’s brother. He stated that his brother ended his life along with his entire family. Jaikishan said, “My brother committed suicide along with his family. It is not yet clear how the deaths occurred. The police were informed and are investigating the matter at the spot.” SSP Shlok Kumar stated that the incident was discovered when the children were not seen in the morning. Upon noticing this, Manish’s brother, who lives in the neighborhood, arrived at the scene. He entered the premises by scaling the main gate. After breaking down the room's door, he found all family members lying dead, following which the police were informed. The police recovered a suicide note written on the wall of the room, which read: "I, Manish, and Seema, are dying of our own free will. The police should not harass anyone." Additionally, a suicide note was found on a piece of paper containing the same message. A video was also discovered on the husband's mobile phone, which he had recorded himself, discussing the suicide. The incident took place in Khapparpur village under the Mahavan police station area. Manish, a resident of Khapparpur, was a farmer. He was married in Madhanai village of Hathras; his wife was the only daughter of her parents. His father-in-law owns three bighas of land, which was intended for Manish. Recently, Manish had sold a plot for ₹19 lakh, out of which ₹12 lakh had already been credited to his account. Manish's father had passed away previously. He has two brothers, Sudhir and Jaikishan, who live right next to his house.

stories.title: UP man strangles girlfriend over refusal to join sex racket:Body dumped on Yamuna Expressway; AI helps police identify 25-year-old victim
stories.summary: A boyfriend murdered his girlfriend by strangling her when she refused to join a sex racket in UP's Agra. After this, he rented a Thar vehicle, put the body in it, and brought it to Agra, about 250 km from Delhi. Then he dumped the body near the Yamuna Expressway and fled. The girlfriend's body was found on February 6, but she could not be identified. Police redeveloped her face with the help of AI. After this, the body was identified as Sonali (25) from Mahoba. During interrogation, it was revealed that she was living in Delhi with her boyfriend, Sunny (28). After this, the police took Sunny into custody on Monday. First, he said that Sonali committed suicide by hanging, but the post-mortem report confirmed murder by strangulation. Upon strict interrogation, Sunny confessed that he had murdered Sonali by strangling her. He revealed that his mother and stepfather also supported him. He wanted to push Sonali into a sex racket, but she was not ready for it. He was afraid that Sonali might tell people and the police about him, which is why he killed her. Sonali insisted on marriage DCP West Aditya Kumar said that during interrogation, Sunny revealed that he is originally from Kanpur. Sunny said that his family had shifted from Kanpur to Mahoba. That's where he met Sonali. Our conversation started, and gradually, friendship turned into love. After this, I went to Delhi with Sonali. Sonali and I started living together in a live-in relationship. Sonali insisted on marrying me, but I didn't want to get married. I had another girlfriend, and I wanted to marry her. She used to threaten - I will tell the police that I am connected to a sex racket Sunny revealed, "I was involved in a sex racket operating in Delhi. I wanted to push Sonali into prostitution, too, but she refused to do so. Sonali had threatened many times that she would tell everyone about my involvement in the sex racket." I was afraid that Sonali might tell everyone about me. So I killed Sonali by strangling her in Burari. After that, I rented a Thar vehicle. At night, I put Sonali's body in that vehicle and left to dispose of it. Couldn't find river so dumped body beside expressway Sunny said, "I thought there would be the Yamuna River in the middle of the Yamuna Expressway, so I would throw the body in it. But I couldn't find any river. So I threw the body on the side of the Yamuna Expressway." After this, I returned to Delhi. I thought the police wouldn't be able to identify the body. The plan was to go to Punjab from Delhi, but police caught me before that. Sonali was married 4 years ago Sonali's brother-in-law, Santkumar, said - Sonali was married four years ago. After marriage, she fell in love with Sunny. Then she left home. Sunny wanted her to do wrong things, but Sonali didn't want to do all this. When Sonali refused to do so, Sunny killed her. Body was found on Yamuna Expressway on February 6 On February 6th at 3:30 PM, villagers grazing goats reached near milestone 148 of the Yamuna Expressway. Near Saurai village, they saw a blanket in the drain. A foul smell was coming from there. Upon going closer, they found a dead body. The villagers informed the guards patrolling the expressway and the police. Around 4 PM, DCP Western Zone Aditya Singh and ACP Etmadpur Devesh Kumar arrived with the SOG team, field unit, and dog squad. AI assistance taken to solve the case Police removed the body from the drain and sent it for a postmortem. The surrounding area was also searched, but nothing related to the deceased's identity was found. Police took help from AI to solve the case. The woman's face was redeveloped using AI. After creating the photo, it was posted at all police stations and social media platforms. Results started coming within 24 hours. The deceased woman was identified as Sonali (25) from Mahoba. After this, the family members filed a murder complaint. Police registered a case and started an investigation. During the investigation, police arrested the accused boyfriend, Sunny.

stories.title: ₹60 lakh lost in gambling:Businessman’s son diagnosed with gambling disorder; addiction comparable to drugs cigarettes
stories.summary: On 7 February, a businessman brought his 19-year-old only son to AIIMS Gorakhpur. The family said the young man was behaving erratically and appeared mentally unstable. According to relatives, the teenager had been playing online games for the past four years and had also been involved in online trading. During this period, he lost nearly ₹60 lakh. He repeatedly demanded money from his father and allegedly threatened to take his own life when refused. Later, he began asking other relatives for money as well. Doctors diagnosed him with gambling disorder, and his treatment is currently underway. Medical experts say that mobile gaming and online trading are often seen as harmless entertainment or an easy way to earn money. However, when the behaviour becomes compulsive and uncontrollable, it can develop into a serious mental health condition. Case raises several important questions: What exactly is gambling disorder? Do online gaming and trading also fall under this category? How dangerous can this condition be for mental health? And how can families recognise the warning signs early, before a hobby turns into an illness? Read all the answers in the Bhaskar Explainer this case from Lucknow In September 2025, 14-year-old Yash committed suicide in Dhanuvasad village of Lucknow due to online gaming addiction. Yash, the only son of Suresh Kumar Yadav, used to play Free Fire game on his father's mobile. He had lost 13 lakh rupees in online gaming. When family members questioned about the missing money from the account, Yash admitted his mistake. Then that same day, he took his life by hanging himself. Question: What is gambling disorder and how dangerous is it? Answer: Gorakhpur AIIMS neuropsychiatrist Dr. Rashid Alam says - gambling disorder is a serious addiction. It is considered a mental health problem. Just like how a person becomes addicted to drugs, similarly in this illness a person becomes addicted to gambling or online gaming. This addiction becomes so severe that even after facing losses, the person cannot stop themselves. They continue gambling constantly. Its effect is not limited to money alone. Gradually, a person's financial condition deteriorates. Relationships become strained and social life is affected. In many cases, the person gets drowned in debt. Their mental as well as physical health starts deteriorating. According to Dr. Rashid Alam, it is as dangerous as alcohol, cigarettes, tobacco, and drug addiction. In this addiction, the person becomes unconscious, then gradually starts falling ill. Just like the craving that occurs with drug use, there is craving in this too. One feels the urge to check their phone and play games repeatedly. They constantly think about that thing. Can't focus on anything else. Question: How do you know if someone is suffering from gambling disorder? Answer: According to Dr. Rashid Alam, Neuro-Psychiatrist at AIIMS Gorakhpur, gambling disorder is a type of behavioral disorder. There are certain criteria to identify it. Question: Do online gaming and trading also fall under this category? Answer: According to mental health experts, when a person spends excessive time continuously on online gaming or trading, cannot stop themselves despite losses, and repeatedly takes risks to recover money, it is considered a gambling disorder. According to Dr. Adarsh Tripathi, Consultant Psychiatrist at KGMU, two to three such patients are coming forward every week who are struggling with addiction to online gaming and trading. The doctor explains that there are many such apps online that trap people by tempting them with promises of higher earnings and wins. In this disorder, the person enters a kind of psychological condition where they cannot accept their losses. To compensate for losses, they keep investing more money repeatedly, which is called the loss recovery trap. In this cycle, they get trapped deeper and deeper. Question: How do people keep getting trapped in this? Answer: Dr. Adarsh Tripathi says that generally no person can continuously win money in gambling apps. These apps hook people by showing them the temptation of winning. Then gradually they trap them in the habit of playing. Many gambling apps use psychological methods to understand user behavior. These apps sense when the user plays more? When they are ready to bet again after a loss? They send offers and notifications accordingly. Many such apps also monitor users' financial activities. This gives them an idea of how much money a person can spend. Because of this, people gradually end up investing more money. They keep getting trapped in this web. Question: What does the study say about gambling disorder? Answer: According to a report published in the medical journal The Lancet, around 80 million young people worldwide are affected by gambling disorder. Due to this mental illness, the person remains constantly stressed. Their mental health deteriorates. Gradually, physical problems also start to emerge. The study showed that gambling disorder is not limited to just financial losses. It leads to increased family disputes. Relationships break down and in many cases suicidal thoughts also emerge. Some people have even shown tendencies towards domestic violence and crime. Gambling addiction can lead a person down wrong and illegal paths. According to the report, the disorder caused by gambling addiction can have long-lasting effects. Without treatment, it becomes difficult to break free from it. Growing trend of different types of gambling The study also revealed that around 80 million people struggling with gambling disorder are involved in some form of gambling. This includes everything from online games played by children and youth on mobile phones to traditional gambling like casinos and betting. According to the report, casinos and real money gaming consume the most money, which can completely ruin many people financially.

stories.title: Businessman father says, 'Son wasn’t driving Lamborghini':Family claims Kanpur Police Commissioner is lying; son is unconscious and admitted in Delhi hospital
stories.summary: Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath has ordered strict action in the case where six people were run over by a Lamborghini car in Kanpur. On Tuesday afternoon, the father of the accused, tobacco businessman K.K. Mishra, visited Gwaltoli police station. Speaking to the media, the father claimed, “My son Shivam Mishra was not driving the car. He was asleep at the time. The vehicle was being driven by the driver, Mohan. After the accident, the car got locked. I will personally bring Shivam to the police station once his health improves.” Responding to the Police Commissioner’s statement that Shivam was driving, the father said, “The Police Commissioner is lying.” Meanwhile, the accused’s lawyer claimed that Shivam is unconscious and admitted to a Delhi hospital. Police have registered an FIR against Shivam Mishra, son of K.K. Mishra. Speaking to the media from Delhi, former UP Chief Minister Akhilesh Yadav said, “The BJP discriminates in delivering justice; they do not ensure fair treatment.” The accident occurred on Sunday afternoon. That night, the police filed an FIR against an unknown driver based on the car number. As the matter gained public attention, the police came under scrutiny. During the investigation, a video emerged showing Shivam being pulled away from the cars driver's seat by his bouncers. Subsequently, the Police Commissioner confirmed Shivam’s name had emerged in the probe, and it was added to the FIR on Monday. On Monday evening, around 5:30 PM, the Police Commissioner placed Gwaltoli station in-charge Santosh Gaud on notice for negligence. After the accident, when the Lamborghini was brought to Gwaltoli police station, it was covered with a black sheet. Immediately after the incident, Station Officer Santosh Gaud had stated that Shivam had fallen ill and was admitted to the hospital. Deputy CM Keshav Maurya said, “Action will be taken against whoever causes an accident.” The 14-crore Lamborghini car (DL-11 CF 4018) involved is registered in Shivam Mishra’s name and is a limited-edition model. Police Commissioner says - complainant did not know Shivam's name Police Commissioner Raghuvir Lal said - FIR has been registered at Gwaltoli police station based on injured Taufiq's complaint in the Lamborghini car accident. Taufiq did not know the name of the accused car driver. Therefore, the accident case was filed based on the car number against an unknown person. The Lamborghini car has been seized. Investigation has revealed that businessman KK Mishra's son Shivam Mishra was driving the car. Now Shivam's name will be added to the FIR. Family members have informed that Shivam Mishra is in the hospital. The police team is now investigating at the businessman's house. Action will be taken based on whatever comes to light. The investigation will also clarify whether Shivam has any medical issues or not. Why was the car covered? On this, the Police Commissioner said that the matter is under investigation. Mohammad Taufiq from Chamanganj Ghusiana stated in the FIR that on February 8 at 1:45 PM, a Lamborghini coming from Parmat on VIP Road hit his parked Bullet and injured him. Several others were also hurt. 5 major police lapses in the case: 1. Released accused without medical check – Shivam Mishra was taken to the station but not medically examined before release; police could not explain the alleged medical emergency. 2. VIP treatment to Lamborghini – The 14-crore car was parked inside the station, covered, and guarded, bypassing standard procedures. 3. FIR filed against unknown driver – Despite Shivam being at the wheel, police initially filed the FIR against an unknown person; his name was added only after 20 hours. 4. No action at accused’s house – Police visited Shivam’s home but returned without completing formalities. 5. Delayed technical inspection – The Lamborghini was not technically inspected, even the day after the accident; station in-charge said experts were awaited. Petition filed in court to release the vehicle Kanpur Police's negligence was taken advantage of by Shivam's lawyer, Mrityunjay Singh. The lawyer filed a petition in ACJM-7 court on Monday for vehicle release and Shivam's bail. The lawyer claims that Shivam was not driving the car; his driver was. However, the Police Commissioner stated that investigation revealed Shivam was driving the car. The court has sought a report from Gwaltoli police station on this petition on Monday itself. Based on the police report, it will be decided whether the vehicle will be released from the station or not and whether the accused will get bail or not. In Kanpur on February 8, tobacco businessman KK Mishra's son Shivam Mishra's Lamborghini car hit more than 6 people. The car hit a Bullet motorcycle rider, who was thrown 10 feet into the air before falling. After this, the Lamborghini climbed on top of the Bullet. After the accident, angry people surrounded the car. According to people, the businessman's son crouched inside the car. After this, his bouncers created a ruckus with people. They tried to chase people away by pushing them. Meanwhile, the police arrived at the scene and brought the car to the police station. At the police station, the businessman's bouncers misbehaved with the victims. After this, people created a huge commotion at the police station. The businessman's son and other injured people have been admitted to a private hospital. Car kept secure inside the police station Eyewitnesses said police took the Lamborghini to the station after the accident, where it was kept secure and covered, due to the influence of the prominent family. Sonu Tripathi, another eyewitness, said he and his cousin Vishal were standing by the roadside on a Bullet motorcycle when the Lamborghini first hit an auto and then crushed their bike. Vishal was thrown far from the collision, and two other boys were also hit, flying about 10 feet onto the footpath. All the injured were sent to hospital. A complaint has been filed at the police station. People said - Accused released from police station due to influence The victims allege that due to influence, the police released accused Shivam Mishra from the police station itself. We were told that Shivam Mishra is sick. Police is pressuring for a forced compromise in the matter. Till late evening, even after the complaint, police did not register a case. Shivam Mishra is fond of luxury cars. He owns several cars. Shivam had invited many Bollywood actors to his son's birthday celebration. He spent crores of rupees on the party. After this, he came under the radar of the Income Tax Department. Businessman's company was raided 2 years ago Tobacco businessman KK Mishra owns a company called Banshidhar Exports Private Limited. This company supplies tobacco to the top gutka companies in Kanpur. About 2 years ago, on February 28, the Income Tax Department raided the company's head office. At that time, cars worth more than 100 crores were found at KK Mishra's Delhi residence. These included luxury cars worth more than 60 crores. There was a 16 crore Rolls-Royce Phantom car, Lamborghini, Ferrari, and a McLaren car. The raid then uncovered tax evasion of more than 100 crores.

stories.title: HDFC bank employee who said 'I am Thakur' breaks silence:Clarifies incident involved ex-employee’s husband, not customer; cites threats online, calls for defamation action
stories.summary: The female bank employee who said, 'I am Thakur, I will teach you a lesson' at HDFC Bank in Kanpur has come forward. Relationship Manager Astha Singh has issued a video giving her clarification. With folded hands, she said- I did not misbehave with any customer. My dispute was with the husband of a female contract employee of the bank. He asked about my caste and misbehaved with me, that's when I got angry. I still stand by my statement. I am a Thakur and I'm proud of it. Actually, Astha's video has been going viral for the past two days. In this, she can be seen hurling abuses. In anger, she is also seen attempting to attack someone by picking up a laptop. However, the viral video is from January 6. Astha is posted at HDFC Bank in Panki. What the female bank employee said in clarification, read here In the released video, Astha said that the video is going viral in the wrong context. The female employee had resigned and demanded immediate relief on the same day. During this time, her sister-in-law was present in the branch since morning, with whom there was a minor argument. She said that later, the female employee told this to her husband, who came to the bank after working hours and used abusive language with me. Astha said that the female employee's husband came to my desk, asked about my caste, and spoke threatening words. 'I stand by my statement' Astha Singh said, I admit that some of my words might be wrong. Words should be chosen carefully in public service, but threats and insulting language cannot be tolerated. The video has been wrongly presented by making it a casteism issue. I stand by my statement. I am a Thakur, and I am proud of it... Jai Shri Ram. 'Threats of rape and cutting hair being made' Additionally, in a conversation with a media channel, Astha said, 'I have forwarded the internal mail to my seniors in this case. Everyone knows that I am not wrong, so we didn't need to take such action in this matter. But when such things are happening, I would definitely want to file a defamation case.' She said, 'After the video went viral, I am being told many things on social media. I am receiving threats of rape and of cutting my hair. Everyone wants to be famous, but not in the wrong way. I am becoming famous in the wrong sense.'

stories.title: Coach attenders selling seats in UP trains:'System' flourishing with connivance of TTEs, who pocket half the money
stories.summary: “Going to Prayagraj? No problem. Lie down here, this is our seat. It will cost Rs 600 for two people. I will give Rs 300 to the TTE, he will stay quiet… won’t say anything. Rs 300 will be his and Rs 300 will be mine,” said an attendant on a train in Uttar Pradesh. In the state, entry into AC coaches is being allowed through bribes. Attendants handle these deals on behalf of the TTE (Travelling Ticket Examiner), so they avoid getting caught. These attendants are outsourced employees, which means the railways cannot take action against them directly. Passenger safety is being badly compromised because seats are being given to anyone without checking ID. This has led to more incidents of bomb threats and luggage theft on trains. Last month, a bomb threat was reported on the Tejas Rajdhani Express (12309) from Patna to New Delhi. The train was stopped in Chandauli, UP. Passengers were evacuated, and all coaches were searched. The spaces assigned to attendants in AC coaches are being sold for money. Hidden Camera Investigation After the Tejas Rajdhani incident, questions arose about train safety. Are IDs being checked for passengers without tickets or with general tickets? To investigate, Dainik Bhaskar sent reporters on two trains. When a seat was requested, the attendant agreed to provide it for a bribe, without checking ID or issuing a fine receipt. It became clear that anyone could enter an AC coach illegally by paying money. First, the reporters checked which trains were crowded. Chambal-Howrah Express (12178) came up because the Magh Mela in Prayagraj was in its final phase. The AC coach showed full status. The reporters took general tickets from Chitrakoot to Prayagraj and asked the TTE for seats. Initially, he refused, but later allowed them to board the AC coach B2. They told the attendant they needed seats to travel to Prayagraj. The attendant offered berths without issuing receipts. Conversation with Attendant Mausam The B2 coach attendant, Mausam, was caught on hidden camera making deals. Reporter: Brother, can you talk to the TTE once, if we can get a seat? Mausam: You won’t get it here… there are two seats outside. Arrangements can be made till Prayagraj. Reporter: Can we lie down? Will you give bedsheets? Mausam: Yes. Reporter: What if the TTE comes and asks? Mausam: No one will ask… this seat is ours. Reporter: We have general tickets. Mausam: No problem. Sit here. From this conversation, it was clear that Mausam was selling his own seat for Rs 300 per passenger. He admitted that the TTE would not interfere and even received a share of the money. Reporter: What if the TTE troubles us? Mausam: I only go till Prayagraj. No problem. Sit comfortably. Mausam also explained that after departure, attendants get a list of empty seats, which they sell. TTEs are aware and receive part of the bribe. Another Case: Dharmendra on Ambedkar Nagar Express On the Prayagraj Dr. Ambedkar Nagar Express (14116), reporters boarded with general tickets to Lalitpur. The attendant, Dharmendra, asked for Rs 700 to provide a berth. He refused to reduce the amount and promised no receipt for the full bribe. Reporter: Is there no TTE? Dharmendra: The TTE knows everything. We get Rs 50 from him and Rs 50 from the passenger. Dharmendra threatened the reporters that the TTE could impose fines if the rules were violated. Despite this, he said passengers could lie down comfortably after paying. He openly admitted the TTE’s involvement and the collection of money. How the System works Attendants sell empty seats and berths for money without checking ID. They collude with TTEs, which is why no receipts are given to passengers. The railway’s claims about safety are false. General ticket holders can easily enter AC coaches. During a nine-hour journey, no railway officer checked what attendants were doing. The attendants have a rate card, charging Rs 300 for every 100 km in the Third AC coach. Safety is ignored, and TTEs profit from the system. Railways aware, promises action Dainik Bhaskar informed DRM Rajnish Agarwal of Prayagraj Rail Division. Division PRO Amit Kumar Singh said they are aware of the problem and urged passengers not to travel without tickets or give space to strangers. DRM Anirudh Kumar of Jhansi Rail Division was also informed about attendants taking bribes. The PRO assured strict action against misconduct. Passengers are advised to report any irregularities, and the railways have promised to take strict action against TTEs and attendants involved in bribery. Now we caught the Prayagraj Dr. Ambedkar Nagar Express (14116) train. It was coming from Prayagraj. We took a general ticket till Lalitpur and boarded coach B2. We traveled for 6 hours in this train. Here we met attendant Dharmendra. He also asked for a Rs 700 bribe to provide a berth. Reporter: Is there no TT? Dharmendra: Where do you want to go? Reporter: I need to go to Lalitpur... Dharmendra: Lalitpur? Reporter: Yes, after Khajuraho station. Dharmendra: Do you have a general ticket? Reporter: Yes. Dharmendra: It will cost Rs 700. Reporter: How much? Dharmendra: Rs 700. The conversation with Dharmendra made it clear that he would charge Rs 700. He won't reduce the amount. No receipt will be given. Now we wanted to know how much the TT's share was in this? In response, Dharmendra said that he only gets Rs 50 from the TT and Rs 50 from the passenger. Dharmendra: If the TT makes it, he will charge more than this... what do you say? Reporter: Rs 700 is too much sir... we have this ticket. Dharmendra: Forget about the ticket. Reporter: The ticket is general class. Dharmendra: TT will add up all the fine-wine. Reporter: If you take Rs 700, will you give a receipt for it? Dharmendra: When TT comes, you can get the receipt. Reporter: If something can be reduced, please do... whatever the system allows? Dharmendra: He will give us Rs 50... it's clear. Now, what can we reduce for you in 50 rupees? Just food costs between Rs 100-200 from here to there. You know this, too. If you eat on the train, it won't cost less than 300. What can you get reduced in that, brother? He'll come after Lalitpur, Khajuraho, right? Reporter: Yes, if not till Lalitpur, then at least till Khajuraho. After Khajuraho, there's only one station left, Lalitpur. Dharmendra: Brother, whether 1 remains or 1 kilometer remains? Reporter: If the seat is booked from Khajuraho, then please give us till Khajuraho. Then we'll stand and travel from there to Lalitpur. Dharmendra: Hey, we will give you a place to sit. When the TT comes, he will finalize it, that's why we're not saying anything. When he comes, he'll make the fine and give it to you. First thing is you've boarded an AC coach. The fine will be higher here. Whenever we talked about reducing the money, attendant Dharmendra threatened to impose a fine. From this, we understood that he would only take Rs 700. Now we wanted to know if a receipt is given for this? In response, Dharmendra said that receipt will be given for half the amount. One seat for 700 rupees, will you travel with the whole family? Reporter: If Rs 700 is paid, then there won't be any fine? Dharmendra: No, there's no fine... Reporter: Will I get this seat or the one inside? Dharmendra: You'll get it... Let's see first... Wherever there's a vacant space, you'll get it. If there's no space here, we'll seat you ahead. What else can we do? Reporter: We are 2 people? Dharmendra: We're talking about one person. What, you think you'll bring the whole family for 700 rupees? Reporter: Will you give at least one seat? Dharmendra: Look, suppose if we don't check the boarding now, how will we know about the space? We'll give you space, tell me then... Or should we lock the door? Reporter: Lock it, then tell us which seat is ours? Dharmendra: Let me know when you want to lie down. This is fully AC. We'll spread the blanket and give you a sheet. You can travel lying down comfortably. Reporter: Don't give the seat like this... give us a proper, good seat. Dharmendra: You can lie down comfortably here. This whole chamber is AC... what do you say? Reporter: Make arrangements inside. Dharmendra: Sit up in this seat... so that we don't go against them, brother. It's clear, we have to get 100 rupees from you and them, 50-50 rupees from both. Look at those sitting in front... they have also paid. Whatever is due, will be received. It's absolutely clear that we will make all arrangements. From attendant Dharmendra's words, we understood that he gives his seat to people in greed for money. However, he has absolutely no concern for the safety of people traveling in AC coach. That's why he didn't even ask for ID proof. Does all this happen with TTE's permission? In response to this, Dharmendra revealed that the TTE knows everything. Dharmendra: The way they make tickets, let's say we get 50-50 rupees. Our work ends right here. We get two-four tickets from here, two-four tickets from there. We leave in the morning, it takes three days. Reporter: Where does the Ambedkar Nagar train start from? Dharmendra: It starts from Prayagraj. It will reach there (Dr. Ambedkar Nagar) tomorrow at 10:30 AM. Then it will depart from there at 11:30 AM. Reporter: Let's sit, but what will we tell if the TTE comes? Dharmendra: No one will say anything, we'll meet from here to the next door. Our duty is in this same coach. Pay when the TT comes, there's nothing to worry about. You know, the TT watches from afar to see who's boarding the compartment. The TT knows everything, who has a ticket... who doesn't. Similarly, we also maintain records. We also get the list, but we don't work without asking. Reporter: Does the TT send this list? Dharmendra: Look at this... the list has arrived. There are three lists here. It's train 14116, see... the list has come... look, what seat number is this? Reporter: This is 8, the lower one is 7. Dharmendra: You sit down; moving back and forth is our job. We'll adjust you. Will take action if TTE-attendants are involved in misconduct We informed DRM Rajnish Agarwal of Prayagraj Rail Division about the irregularities happening in trains. Division PRO Amit Kumar Singh said - We know that seats are not available in any train these days. Passengers should also be mindful of their safety and the rules. They should not travel without tickets. Do not give space to strangers on your seat. Passengers should inform us that strict action will be taken We informed DRM Anirudh Kumar of Jhansi Rail Division about the attendant taking money. The PRO assured strict action.

stories.title: 22-year-old designer dies while watching web series in Meerut:Stumbled getting out of bed; doctors confirm brain vessel rupture
stories.summary: 'Kaif was a very good child. He took care of the family's needs, but he used to watch mobile a lot; now my child has gone to Allah.' While saying all this, tears welled up in Mohammad Kaif's mother, Tasleem's eyes. Composing herself, she said, he was very straightforward, respected everyone, and never made eye contact while talking to anyone. On the night of February 6, he was watching a web series on his mobile in his room. Suddenly, he felt uneasy. He got up from the bed, then fell to the ground. The family took him to 3 private hospitals in Meerut, then showed him at Safdarjung Hospital in Delhi, where he died. Under what circumstances did 22-year-old Kaif die? To find this out, the Dainik Bhaskar team reached Khairnagar. Read the report... Father is property dealer, family has been living on rent for 8 years Kaif lived with his family in a rented house in Guler Wali Gali. His family had shifted to this house 8 years ago. Kaif's father, Farooq, works in property dealing. The family includes his mother Tasleem, 1 daughter, and son Kaif. The daughter is married, and Kaif used to do computer designing. He would leave for office every day at 9 AM, then return only at 8:30 PM. After having dinner, he would go to sleep. According to the family, during this time, he would watch movies, web series, and sometimes play games on mobile till midnight. The family said that before 2019, he used to play PUBG game, but after it was banned, he only played normal games on mobile. He also had a hobby of making reels. Now know what happened on February 6 Kaif returned home by 8 PM after work, had dinner, and later went for a walk with his friend Shoaib. Around 11:30 PM, Shoaib dropped him off at home. Kaif went to bed but kept using his mobile with headphones. About an hour later, he became confused, got up, and stumbled, falling on the floor. His family rushed to his aid after hearing the fall. Farooq, a relative, said Kaif was hitting his head and seemed to be in severe pain. He took Kaif to several hospitals, starting with Hope Hospital, where no doctor was available. They then went to Sushila Jaswant Rai and Saket’s private hospital, but the staff focused on billing rather than treatment. Eventually, an employee informed them that Kaif’s condition was serious and advised taking him to Delhi. Admitted with difficulty in Delhi Farooq says - Meerut hospital did not give a referral letter, due to which Kaif was not admitted to Delhi AIIMS and GB Pant Hospital. With great difficulty, Kaif was admitted to Safdarjung Hospital, after which Kaif's treatment could begin. However, after a few hours, Kaif passed away. The father alleges that if treatment had been received on time, Kaif would have survived. He returned to Meerut with Kaif and buried him that night itself. Brother said - Treatment was delayed, otherwise brother would have survived After Mohammad Kaif's health deteriorated, his cousin brother Osama also kept running between hospitals. Osama said - if Kaif had received treatment early, he would have survived. First one, then two, and then the third hospital referred Kaif to Delhi without even checking his medical condition. The biggest issue was that they didn't even provide a referral letter, due to which after facing disappointment from two hospitals there, Kaif was finally admitted to Safdarjung Hospital, but by then it was too late. Now, know Kaif's medical history too Kaif was only 22 years old, but when he was taken to the hospital, his blood pressure had gone above 300. According to the doctor, the blood vessels in his brain burst due to high blood pressure. Kaif had high blood pressure problems 10 years ago in 2016. Since then, he had been cautious about BP. He was taking medicines too, but still couldn't prevent the pressure building up in his brain. Now hear from the shop owner where Kaif used to work... Shop owner said - Kaif did not use mobile phone here Kaif was a graphic designer by profession; he used to prepare designs for printing. He worked at Sheikh Meraj's shop. He says Kaif worked very honestly. As far as mobile usage is concerned, it is our office rule that no one can use a mobile here to maintain work quality, so Kaif did not it. When he left the shop at 8:30 PM on February 6, he was completely fine.

stories.title: Terrorist Abdul Rehman killed inside Faridabad jail:Ram Temple conspiracy accused stabbed by co-prisoner; family was told health deteriorated
stories.summary: Abdul Rehman, the terrorist who conspired to bomb Ayodhya's Ram Temple, was killed in Faridabad jail (Haryana). His fellow inmate, Arun Chaudhary alias Abu Jat, attacked him with a sharp object in the jail's high-security barrack. The 20-year-old terrorist Abdul was arrested by the Gujarat ATS in March 2025. Investigation revealed that he was in contact with notorious Al-Qaeda in Indian Subcontinent (AQIS) terrorist Abu Sufian. After the terrorist's murder, women at Abdul's house in Milkipur (Ayodhya) began wailing. However, they were told that Abdul had been admitted to the hospital in serious condition. Abdul has had a hole in his heart since childhood, and his health suddenly deteriorated. On the morning of February 9, the village head's son, Kailash Jaiswal, received a call from the Faridabad jail administration. The jail official informed him that Abdul had died. Please send their family to Faridabad as soon as possible so that further procedures can be carried out. After this, Abdul's father, Abu Bakr, and his uncle Usman have left from Ayodhya for Faridabad. They will bring Abdul's body to Ayodhya. He will be buried in a cemetery here. Dainik Bhaskar digital app team reached Milkipur, 45 km away from Ayodhya. Read the report… Mother not told about murder, told - health deteriorated, treatment ongoing Bhaskar team reached Chamanganj Road after traveling 5km inside from the Ayodhya-Raebareli highway link road. Abu Bakr has a 650-square-foot house here. A wooden plank was lying outside the house. Some women were sitting on it. They were crying bitterly. Some women were sitting on the ground and crying. Some women were consoling them. These women included grandmother, mother, and aunt (maternal aunt). People from the neighborhood had gathered around. We were not allowed to talk to the women. Abdul Rehman's uncle, Israr, said - The women have not yet been told about Abdul's death. They have been told that Abdul's health deteriorated, so he had to be admitted to the hospital. He has a hole in his heart, and he has been treated in many hospitals in Ayodhya. Medicines were also continued in jail. Get my son out of jail, show me his face We tried to listen to what Abdul's crying mother, Ashmeen. She was crying and saying - We had just met him in jail, don't know how... what happened to him? Show me his face once. Get my child out of jail so that he can be treated. Abdul's uncle Israr says - On Thursday, that is Jumma night, Abdul's father and mother went to jail to meet him. There Abdul was sitting on one side of the glass, while my brother-in-law and sister were seated on the other side. They talked over phone. Sister had taken some food items for Abdul, but it was not permitted to give them to the prisoner. Father Abu's mobile was switched off, so called the village head The uncle said the family was in touch with a lawyer to secure Abdul’s bail and had filed a petition in a Faridabad court. However, the incident occurred before any relief could come through. “We just wanted the child to come out of jail,” he said. Explaining how they learnt about the incident, he said that on February 9 at around 9:30 am, the village head’s son, Kailash Jaiswal, received a call from the jail. Abdul’s phone was switched off, so jail authorities informed him instead. Inside Abdul’s modest home are two small rooms. The family sleeps in one room, while cooking is done in a corner of the courtyard. Household essentials are kept in the second room. There is also a small room on the roof where the family prays. Outside the house is a chicken shop run by Abdul’s father, Abu Bakr, which has mostly remained closed since Abdul’s arrest. The family survives in poverty and holds an Antyodaya ration card. Abdul’s mother, Ashmin, lives with her three daughters, all younger than him. An e-rickshaw parked outside the house was Abdul’s livelihood before his arrest. How terrorist Abdul was caught? Caught on March 2, 2025 with help of Gujarat ATS, IB Terrorist Abdul Rehman (19) was arrested on March 2 by the Haryana Police Special Task Force in Faridabad with the assistance of Gujarat ATS and the central intelligence agency IB. During the arrest, investigators recovered two live hand grenades from his possession, which were later safely defused by a bomb disposal squad. Abdul Rahman, a resident of Milkipur in Uttar Pradesh, was found to be running multiple social media accounts. Investigators said several videos related to the Ram Temple were recovered from his devices. He had allegedly been uploading inflammatory content online for around one and a half years. Abdul initially used TikTok to post such videos and later shifted to Instagram after TikTok was banned in India. Abdul caught Abu Sufyan's attention through inflammatory videos Abdul Rehman also started posting many inflammatory videos and speeches on Instagram. Due to this, his Instagram account was taken down multiple times. After seeing the inflammatory videos, Abdul caught the attention of terrorist Abu Sufyan. After this, Al-Qaeda in the Indian Sub-continent (AQIS) started brainwashing Abdul Rehman and providing online terrorism training. Came on investigation agencies' radar through social media Abdul Rehman came under the radar of investigation agencies after repeated strikes on his account. Haryana STF, Gujarat STF, and UP STF started tracking him. Abu Sufian had hidden 2 hand grenades and detonators in a pit in Faridabad through his handler. After this, he was directed to go to Ayodhya on April 4, but he was caught by Gujarat ATS and Haryana STF on March 2 itself. Case registered against Abdul under these sections Based on the STF inspector's statement, an FIR was registered against terrorist Abdul Rehman at Dabua police station in Faridabad under sections 25(1)(A) Arms Act, sections 4(A), 4(B), 5 of the Explosive Substances Act 1908, along with the Explosive Act. After arrest, Gujarat ATS produced him in court, where he was remanded for 10 days. After getting custody, the Gujarat ATS took the terrorist Abdul with them. Subsequently, other investigation procedures were carried out from there. 3 important points about the prisoner who killed the terrorist...
