stories.title: Wanted criminal fires several rounds at SP, killed in encounter:Amjad looted in police uniform; kept shooting in Muzaffarnagar till bullets run out
stories.summary: Police in Muzaffarnagar shot dead Amjad, a criminal carrying a reward of Rs 50,000, in an encounter. At around 3.30 am on Thursday, police received information that he was heading towards his village. Acting on the tip-off, police laid a cordon. The police team repeatedly warned him to surrender, but he began indiscriminate firing with a carbine and a pistol. A total of 20 rounds were fired from the accused’s side. SP Rural Aditya Bansal, CO Gajendra Singh and Station House Officer Subhash Atri narrowly escaped. Bullets struck their bulletproof jackets. Sub-Inspector Sandeep Chaudhary and Constable Ashfaq were shot in the hand. Police then retaliated with four rounds of fire. During the exchange, Amjad was hit by a bullet and fell to the ground. Police lifted him and took him to their vehicle, then rushed him to Budhana CHC, where he died during treatment. However, his accomplice managed to escape under the cover of darkness. The encounter took place in the Budhana police station area. The 40-year-old Amjad was a resident of Shahpur in Muzaffarnagar. Around 40 cases were registered against him in Uttar Pradesh, Rajasthan, Delhi and Uttarakhand. In 2021, he had looted 5 kg of gold from Muthoot Finance in Churu, Rajasthan. He often carried out crimes wearing a police uniform. He had recently committed a robbery in the Budhana police station area, and police were searching for him in connection with that case. Criminal kept firing until he ran out of bullets According to initial information, the encounter lasted around 20–25 minutes. The miscreant kept firing at police personnel until the bullets in both his pistol and carbine were exhausted. His bullets also struck vehicles at the scene, shattering their windows. Police personnel took cover behind a vehicle to save their lives and returned fire. The police recovered a carbine, a motorcycle and a pistol from the spot. Created terror in Muzaffarnagar and Ghaziabad Amjad was a wanted criminal not only in Uttar Pradesh but also in Delhi, Rajasthan, Haryana, Uttarakhand and Bihar. A total of 40 cases were registered against him. He had particularly created terror in Muzaffarnagar and Ghaziabad in Uttar Pradesh. Of these, 21 cases were registered in Muzaffarnagar and nine in Ghaziabad. Apart from this, two cases were lodged in Bijnor, one in Meerut, one in Ghazipur, one in Bihar, one in Rajasthan, two in Delhi and one in Noida. Entered crime world in 2012, carried out robberies wearing police uniform Amjad stepped into the world of crime in 2012. Within just a year, he had created such fear that by 2013 he was booked under the Gangster Act at New Mandi police station in Muzaffarnagar and at Kotwali Gangnahar in Haridwar. He carried out robberies while wearing a police uniform and would open fire immediately if anyone resisted. In 2017, he came into the spotlight after shooting dead a youth during an attempted robbery. Besides this, four cases of attempt to murder are also registered against him. SSP Sanjay Kumar Verma said— Around 3 am, there was an encounter with the hardened criminal Amjad. The criminal, who carried a reward of Rs 50,000, was injured in police firing. He died during treatment at the Community Health Centre. A total of 40 cases are registered against him. Apart from Uttar Pradesh, he was also wanted in Haryana, Bihar, Rajasthan and Uttarakhand. 20 criminals killed in 130 days in UP CM had said – ‘If UP Police do not shoot, should they take the bullets instead?’ On February 3, during the inauguration of UP Pharma Conclave 1.0, Yogi said that more than 900 riots took place in Uttar Pradesh between 2012 and 2017. It was at such a time that he was given responsibility. “We decided on zero tolerance. Many times people comment on why the police fired. If the police do not fire, should they take the bullets instead? If that criminal has the freedom to shoot, we have also given pistols to the police.” ‘UP Police carrying out encounters for praise and promotion’ Last week, the Allahabad High Court expressed strong displeasure over the ‘half encounter’ method of the UP Police. The court observed that police officers were firing unnecessarily merely for appreciation, premature promotion and praise on social media. The High Court issued guidelines on six points. The bench of Justice Arun Kumar Deshwal clearly warned that if Supreme Court guidelines are not followed in encounter cases, the district SP, SSP and Police Commissioner will be held personally guilty of contempt of court. 259 criminals killed in encounters in eight years According to the state government, from March 2017 to October 2025, the UP Police have killed 259 criminals in encounters. During this period, more than 15,000 police encounters took place, in which over 31,000 criminals were arrested and more than 10,000 were shot.

stories.title: Groom found to be transgender after wedding:Barabanki bride’s family detains groom, baraat returns without bride
stories.summary: Shock and confusion gripped a village in Barabanki district on Friday after the groom was allegedly discovered to be transgender shortly after completing the wedding rituals. The incident took place under the Kothi police station limits and led to panic, anger and dramatic developments at the venue. According to reports, the wedding procession had arrived amid music and celebrations, and the bride’s family welcomed the guests warmly. Rituals such as the garland exchange and the seven sacred pheras were completed without any suspicion. The bride’s farewell ceremony was scheduled for the following morning. However, the situation took an unexpected turn shortly before the farewell when a group of transgender persons arrived at the venue to collect the customary ‘neg’ (traditional gift given during weddings). Rs 23,000 payment attempt raises suspicion among bride’s family Members of the transgender group reportedly recognised the groom immediately. In what appeared to be an attempt to prevent disclosure, the groom’s family quickly offered Rs 23,000 and requested them to remain silent. This sudden payment raised suspicion among the bride’s relatives. When the bride’s family demanded verification, the groom allegedly refused and attempted to flee the venue. At that point, members of the transgender group revealed that the groom himself was transgender and had previously lived with their community. The groom was identified as Rishu (22), son of Bhagyachandra, a resident of Pure Ganai village in Dinauna area under Ram Sanehi Ghat. The marriage had been arranged around six months ago, and the wedding was held on February 13. Guests flee, groom detained by bride’s relatives As the news spread, chaos erupted at the venue. Several members of the groom’s family quietly fled, while more than half of the wedding guests left the lodging area. Enraged relatives of the bride detained the groom. Although police reached the spot, no formal complaint was filed. Sources said the families avoided legal action due to social stigma and fear of public embarrassment. The bride’s family later served refreshments to the remaining guests. The groom’s family agreed to compensate the wedding expenses, and after paying the amount, the wedding procession returned without the bride. Transgender community intervenes, takes groom away Later, members of the transgender community intervened and freed the groom from the bride’s family’s custody, taking him away with them. They stated that the groom had previously lived with their group and was part of their troupe, where he used to play the dholak. The bride’s uncle said the marriage had been arranged in good faith and the family was unaware of the truth. He added that the groom had been adopted by his maternal aunt and raised by her since childhood. The bride’s family had agreed to the alliance based on his appearance and assurances that he owned two bighas of land. They believed their daughter would have a secure and stable future.

stories.title: Sitapur BJP MLA tells SHO ‘know your limits’:Sits on protest at police station; demands action within 24 hours
stories.summary: BJP MLA Gyan Tiwari lashed out at police over their action and staged a sit-in protest at Rampur Mathura police station on Sunday afternoon. He arrived at around 1 pm with his supporters and sat on the ground inside the station premises. During this time, a heated argument broke out between Station House Officer (SHO) Sanjay Pandey and the MLA. The inspector said, “Sir, I will leave the police station, I will go.” The MLA replied angrily, “What do you mean you will leave? Is it your property? You will not leave on your own, you will be removed. Do you think you are doing us a favour? Know your limits. Show us by resigning.” Circle Officer (CO) Mahmoodabad Ved Prakash intervened and took the MLA aside to calm him down. The MLA said the police had ruined the lives of poor people through their actions. He also expressed anger at head constable Ravishankar Yadav and constable Vinod Yadav posted at the station. The MLA alleged that late Saturday night, the police forcibly shut down a ‘nautanki’ (folk theatre) programme and took action ignoring the rules. Around two hours later, Superintendent of Police (SP) Ankur Agarwal spoke to the MLA over the phone and assured him that action would be taken within 24 hours. Only after this assurance did the MLA agree to end his protest. To pacify the MLA, the station in-charge even sat on the ground. After the argument, he later got up and left, while the Circle Officer remained present at the scene. MLA stages protest, demands action against police staff On Sunday afternoon, the BJP MLA reached Rampur Mathura police station with his supporters and began protesting while sitting on the ground. CO Ved Prakash assured him of an inquiry and action, but the MLA remained firm on his demands. He said his protest would continue until action was taken against the station in-charge, head constable, and constable. The MLA levelled serious allegations against the police, saying their behaviour had created fear and resentment among the public. He warned that if action was not taken against the guilty officers, he would raise the issue at higher levels. He also accused the station in-charge of acting arbitrarily and targeting BJP workers unfairly. ASP ordered to investigate the matter During the protest, a large crowd gathered at the police station, creating chaos for some time. Additional police forces were deployed to control the situation. The incident is related to the Rampur Mathura police station area, and officials have been directed to prepare a detailed report. At around 3 pm, the MLA got up from the ground and sat on a chair. The Circle Officer facilitated a phone conversation between the MLA and SP Ankur Agarwal, who assured him that an inquiry would be completed and action taken within 24 hours. Following this assurance, the MLA ended his protest and left with his supporters. SP Ankur Agarwal said that ASP South Durgesh Singh has been assigned to investigate the matter, and further action will be taken based on the inquiry report.

stories.title: Sugar mill worker hangs himself over ₹2.5 lakh debt:Family protests at mill gate; demands justice, job for deceased’s son
stories.summary: An employee of Anamika Sugar Mill in Bulandshahr died by suicide after hanging himself. In his note, he wrote, “There isn’t even flour at my home.” The employee was identified as Sharif (50), a resident of Agaota. After his death, family members and villagers placed the body on the road and staged a blockade. They also protested at the mill gate. Sharif used to take pesticides from the mill to sell, and he reportedly owed the mill ₹2.5 lakh. On receiving information about the protest, Circle Officer Prakhar Pandey reached the spot with police force and pacified the protesters. The body was then sent for post-mortem. First read the suicide note… “To all family members, brothers, sisters, relatives and acquaintances, Assalamualaikum. Please forgive me. After me, take care of my family and my daughters. They have no one except me. I am taking this step under great compulsion. Allah Hafiz…” Now read the full matter in detail Sharif had been working at the mill for the past 20 years. His family accused the mill management of mentally harassing him. They alleged that an official, Neeraj Ujjwal, was pressuring him to deposit payment for medicines distributed to farmers and threatening to sack him if he failed. The family demanded a job for the deceased’s son and financial assistance. CO Prakhar Pandey said a complaint has been taken from the family. All their issues will be addressed and they will get justice. Meanwhile, mill chairman Jitendra Singh said the management was not at fault in the suicide case, though they sympathise with the bereaved family and will provide whatever help possible. Had to deposit 2.5 lakhs in the mill Social worker Rahees from Agaota said Sharif used to distribute pesticides from the mill to farmers. The management was pressuring him to deposit ₹2.5 lakh, which forced him into this step. He demanded strict legal action against those responsible and a job for a family member. Congress posted the incident on social media The incident was also shared from the social media handle of Indian National Congress. The post said that struggling with financial hardship, Mohammad Sharif wrote in his note that there wasn’t even flour at home and then took his life. It added that the incident shows the hardships people are facing and how even basic needs are unmet, alleging the government is busy polishing its image through publicity. During the protest, villagers raised slogans against the mill owner. District Congress president Ziaurrahman reached the spot, met the bereaved family, expressed condolences and provided rations. He demanded strict action against the mill management and said the party would raise its voice at every level to secure justice for the family.

stories.title: UP Evening Wrap:Om Birla to attend Tarique Rahman’s oath ceremony in Bangladesh; skull garlands, firebursts at Shiv Baraat in Varanasi
stories.summary: Bhaskar English brings you the biggest news from Uttar Pradesh and around the world. Here are the top news headlines of the day: 1. 24 Super Rafales also part of India’s 114 Rafale deal; IAF to upgrade jets from F-3 to advanced F-4, F-5 India is set to finalise a ₹3.25 lakh crore deal with France for 114 Rafale fighter jets. French President Emmanuel Macron will begin his three-day visit to India on 17 February, during which the agreement is expected to be sealed. Out of the 114 aircraft, 24 will be ‘Super Rafale’ jets. These are being developed by French aerospace company Dassault Aviation under the F-5 variant. 2. Skull garlands and fire bursts amaze devotees: Artists dressed as spirits dazzle onlookers at Shiv Baraat Over a million worshippers gathered at Kashi Vishwanath Dham for Mahashivratri rituals, forming 5-km queues as foreign visitors joined. Security tightened with ATS teams and drones, while in Prayagraj up to two million prepared for Magh Mela’s final holy dip. 3. Cricketer commits suicide after shooting girlfriend in Noida: Caste opposition and family pressure culminate in tragedy On Valentine’s Day in Noida, police found a couple dead inside a locked car with a pistol and shells. Investigators say the man shot the woman before killing himself. A prior note revealed family opposition to their relationship over caste and career issues. 4. PM Modi invited to Tarique Rahman’s oath ceremony; Meeting with Macron same day likely to block Dhaka visit Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) Chairman Tarique Rahman will be sworn in as the country’s new Prime Minister on 17 February. Breaking from tradition, the ceremony will be held at the South Plaza of the Jatiya Sangsad Bhaban in Dhaka instead of the Presidential Palace. Dhaka has invited several regional leaders, including Prime Minister Narendra Modi, to attend the ceremony. However, there has been no official confirmation from India so far. 5. Panchayat elections to be held after UP Assembly polls: OBC Commission report may take 6 months, political parties yet to begin preparations Uttar Pradesh panchayat elections may be postponed as government told Allahabad High Court it will form OBC panel. Minister Om Prakash Rajbhar insists polls on time, but parties including Bharatiya Janata Party reportedly favour delay until after 2027 Assembly polls. 6. Shankaracharya raises concern over safety threats: Says, 'How can I ask security from those plotting my murder' Swami Avimukteshwaranand denied allegations after Ashutosh Brahmachari accused him in court. The Allahabad High Court reserved its verdict on whether to order an FIR, while the seer called charges ideological and politically driven. Decision is due February 21 following hearings. 7. 50+ global CEOs to attend India AI Impact Summit 2026 For the five days coming week, New Delhi won’t just be India’s political capital, it will be one of the most important AI capitals in the world. The India AI Impact Summit 2026 begins on February 16 and runs until February 20 at Bharat Mandapam. The event is expected to bring together some of the biggest names in artificial intelligence, along with world leaders, policymakers, and startup founders. Simply put, if AI is shaping the future, many of the people building that future will be in the same room. 8. Varanasi’s Noor Fatima builds Rudreshwar Mahadev temple: Performs puja alongside namaz, says, 'shattered after husband’s death, Bholenath supported me' Senior advocate Noor Fatima of Varanasi built the Rudreshwar Mahadev Temple after recurring dreams and her husband’s death. The Muslim lawyer says faith in Lord Shiva guides her, while residents praise the shrine as a living example of communal harmony. 9. 'You are Dalit, I am OBC’: Girlfriend refuses marriage, heartbroken man dies by suicide after final meeting; mother files FIR against her “My son was deeply in love with Saumya. He used to say he was the hero of Aashiqui 2. She was his entire world. But Saumya loved his money, not him. As long as he was earning well, everything was fine. The moment he lost his job, she began distancing herself. She refused to marry him, saying, ‘You are Dalit, and I am OBC.’ My son could not bear the heartbreak and ended his life.” These are the words of Kiran Pakhare, mother of Tushar Pakhare, who died by suicide in Jhansi on February 6. 10. Kedarnath Dham to open from April 22 onwards The doors of Kedarnath Dham will reopen for devotees on April 22, 2026, at 8 am. The auspicious date and timing were calculated and officially announced on the occasion of Mahashivratri at the Omkareshwar Temple, Ukhimath, the winter seat (Panch Kedar Gaddi Sthal) of Lord Kedarnath in Rudraprayag district.

stories.title: SP leader dies after pole crashes onto moving car:1,000-kg structure jolts vehicle 2 feet up in Pratapgarh accident
stories.summary: A one-ton high-mast light pole fell onto a moving car in Pratapgarh, killing a Samajwadi Party leader on the spot before he could even cry out. The pole crashed onto the driver’s side front portion, lifting the rear of the car about two feet into the air. The incident occurred around 1 pm on Sunday at Babuganj market in the Antu area. A video of the accident has surfaced. Workers were installing a high-mast light outside a Bharat Petroleum outlet when the pole suddenly lost control and toppled. At the time, SP leader Lal Bahadur Yadav (47) was driving his Creta towards the city. He had contested the 2022 election from Antu Nagar Panchayat. He was also a PWD contractor and held a country liquor licence. Now read the full case… Lal Bahadur was the eldest among three brothers and one sister. He is survived by four daughters and a son, the youngest child. His father, Bade Lal Yadav, has passed away. His youngest brother is a lawyer, while the middle brother farms in the village. His only younger sister had been married on 4 February, and his maternal uncle’s daughter was married on Saturday night. He had returned home in the morning and was leaving for Pratapgarh when the accident happened. Car was moving fast as pole fell from above The entire incident was captured on CCTV from a bungalow near the petrol pump. In the 14-second clip, the car can be seen moving at speed as the pole falls from above and crashes onto its front side within seconds. Lal Bahadur lived in Babuganj market and was heading towards the city at about 1 pm. He had barely travelled a short distance from home when the high-mast pole fell onto his car. The impact lifted the rear of the vehicle into the air and crushed the front completely. He got trapped between the seat and the pole. People nearby shifted the pole and pulled him out. He could not speak. He was taken to hospital, where doctors declared him dead after examination. After the incident, a crowd gathered at the spot. Police investigation suggests negligence during installation may have caused the accident. The heavy pole struck the front portion of the car, and CCTV footage shows the rear lifting nearly two feet. Pole was being erected without proper safety measures Panic spread in the area after the incident. Police reached the scene and began an investigation. Preliminary findings indicate possible negligence during installation. The body has been sent for post-mortem, and authorities say action will be taken against those responsible.

stories.title: Lathi charge on farmers in Ghaziabad:Clash with police during protest against dumping ground; angry crowd pelts stones
stories.summary: There was chaos in Ghaziabad on Sunday over a dumping ground in Tronica City. Farmers were holding a protest against the construction of the site when a clash broke out between them and the police. According to reports, the police tried to remove the protesters by force and put them into vehicles. This made the farmers angry. Soon, some people in the crowd started throwing stones. To control the situation, the police carried out a lathi-charge. Many people were injured in the clash, including women and elderly villagers. An elderly woman fainted during the incident. Villagers claimed that around 50 to 60 people were hurt. One woman suffered a serious head injury, while another villager reportedly fractured his hip. The farmers said they were protesting peacefully for their demands. They claimed that a dumping ground would spread foul smell in the area and cause health problems. They demanded that a school or hospital should be built on the land instead of a garbage First, see 4 pictures A heated argument broke out between farmers-villagers protesting against the dumping ground and the police in Mirpur Hindu village, Tronica City police station area. The situation escalated when the police lathi-charged the protesting villagers to disperse them. Many farmers, women, and elderly people were injured in this action. Villagers say that they were protesting peacefully. Then, the police suddenly started forcibly putting people into vehicles. When women protested, they were also lathi-charged. A woman said that an elderly woman suffered a serious head injury. Meanwhile, there is also news of a villager's hip being fractured. Many others have also sustained injuries. Manoj from Panchayra village said that they were sitting on a protest only for their demands, but the police lathi-charged without warning. Vineet Sharma said - 50 to 60 villagers were injured in this lathi-charge. Male police officers also used force on women. The formation of a dumping ground spreads foul smell in the area and increases the risk of diseases. A school or hospital should be built on this land, not a garbage dumping site. Currently, there is a tense atmosphere in the village and heavy police force has been deployed. No official statement has been released by the administration regarding this matter yet. People from many villages are protesting Farmers from Pachayra, Badarpur, Meerpur in Tronica City are continuously protesting against the dumping ground. Even before, there have been several altercations between farmers and the police during protests here. Farmers broke the lock and entered Today, farmers and local residents in Meerpur, Tronica City area, were supposed to submit a memorandum to the administration. They broke the lock and entered this dumping ground. During this, ACP Loni Siddharth Gautam arrived at the spot with forces from 4 police stations. ACP Siddharth Gautam stated that an attempt was made to explain to the farmers. Despite this, people did not comply, after which they created a ruckus and pelted stones. 2 policemen were injured in this. Both these policemen have been sent to the hospital. Its video has also surfaced. The police used mild force to disperse the crowd. Further action is being taken in this regard.

stories.title: Sister-in-law murdered after marriage refusal:Accused attempts suicide in Mathura, wed 4 months ago
stories.summary: A younger brother allegedly killed his elder brother’s wife after she refused his marriage proposal and later attempted suicide. Both were found seriously injured by family members and taken to hospital by ambulance. The woman died during treatment, while the accused remains critical. Police reached the scene after receiving information from the hospital and questioned relatives about the incident. The case is from Sunday in the Nauhjheel area. Woman's sister had rejected Deepak for marriage Jwala Prasad lives in Kateliya Bagai with his two sons, Deepak (23) and Kalu. Four months ago, Kalu married Karishma in a mass wedding ceremony held in Baldev. Deepak had also attended the ceremony. During the event, Karishma chose Kalu, while her sister reportedly rejected Deepak’s proposal. Since then, Deepak was said to be upset with his sister-in-law and her family. First killed the girl, then cut his own throat On Sunday afternoon, Kalu and his father were working in the fields. During that time, Deepak allegedly argued with Karishma over an issue. In a fit of anger, he is accused of killing her and then attempting suicide with a blade. SSP said - attempt was made to destroy evidence Senior Superintendent of Police Shlok Kumar said the hospital informed authorities that a young man and a woman had been brought in with serious injuries. During treatment, the woman died, while the युवक remains in critical condition. After the information, police inspected the house. A blade was found in stove ashes and appeared to have been cleaned. Mattresses had been washed and left to dry on the roof. Officers suspect an attempt was made to destroy evidence after the incident. The deceased woman was a resident of Agra. Her family has been informed, and the case is under investigation.

stories.title: Lucknow’s air is bad too, says Akhilesh Yadav:Brings Naseemuddin to office, inducts him into SP
stories.summary: A senior Muslim leader in western UP, Naseemuddin Siddiqui, has joined the Samajwadi Party. On Sunday, Akhilesh Yadav arrived with him at the party office in Lucknow, where he was formally inducted. Along with Siddiqui, 15,758 people also joined SP, most of whom were former workers of the Bahujan Samaj Party. Akhilesh, reacting to Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath’s population remark, said people in Lucknow claim Delhi’s air is bad, but the truth is both places have bad air. He also mentioned the Codeine cough syrup case and asked, “Where is Codeine brother?” After joining SP, Siddiqui said he is the most junior in the party and everyone else is his senior. He added that in whichever party he worked, he always considered Akhilesh his leader. “You never spoke only for Hindus, Muslims, Sikhs or Christians, you spoke for everyone,” he said, before reciting a couplet about moving forward with the whole world together. Targeting the state government, he said their aim is precise—to change power and make Akhilesh Chief Minister in 2027. He alleged crime is at its peak and claimed that if one speaks too much, bulldozers are used. He then recited another couplet describing a time of destruction and injustice. Siddiqui had resigned from the Indian National Congress on 24 January. It was speculated he might join Azad Samaj Party led by Chandrashekhar Azad or form his own party and ally with it. However, equations changed and last Friday he confirmed he would join SP. Having started his political career with BSP, Siddiqui had served as a cabinet minister in the government of Mayawati. He is regarded as a major Muslim face in UP politics. After Azam Khan went to jail, SP lacked a Muslim leader of similar stature, which the party now hopes to address through Siddiqui. Now read Akhilesh’s key statements— 1- ‘Naseemuddin is a veteran leader, has experience running several governments’ Akhilesh said Siddiqui is an experienced leader who has worked with multiple governments. He also welcomed Anees Ahmad Khan, Raj Kumar Pal, Deenanath Kushwaha and Danish into the party. He said ties between the Bahujan community and SP are growing stronger, which will increase unity. He added that before Holi Milan, they are holding a PDA Holi gathering, and this joining is important because it will strengthen PDA’s victory prospects. He recalled how B. R. Ambedkar and Ram Manohar Lohia once tried to unite, with alliances forming and breaking repeatedly, and expressed hope of taking that struggle forward. 2- ‘Some people are even insulting Shankaracharya’ Without naming the CM, Akhilesh said, “What can you expect from them? They are insulting our Shankaracharya. Will you bring a new law for this too? Everyone can see it happening openly. Do we have the stature to speak against Shankaracharya?” He also referred to remarks made about Leader of Opposition Mata Prasad Pandey, a former Speaker, saying everyone heard them. He claimed these people are afraid of Gen-Z and added that one youngster joked CM can also mean “corrupt mouth.” 3- ‘The Chief Minister is a player, but unable to play’ Akhilesh said SP’s works are being copied. Ten years ago, SP showed its vision by landing an aircraft on an expressway, and today the country is moving along that vision. “The Chief Minister is a player, but unable to play,” he said. He alleged that only trucks with the same number are being caught for overloading and that grease was even found on some number plates. He said sometimes the government seizes string, sometimes cannabis, and a spelling change makes it something else. He added that even incidents of a bull entering public hearings have surfaced. In one case, 370 kg of cannabis was being transported in a modified truck in cinematic style, while elsewhere 10 kg was seized. “The real question is not that it was seized, but where it was going,” he said. 4- ‘Demonetisation was brought to remove SP’ Referring again to the CM’s Delhi population remark, Akhilesh said talk has now begun about bad air. Lucknow residents say Delhi’s air is bad, but in reality both are bad. He said UP decides the country’s direction and claimed demonetisation was introduced to remove SP. The CM had said in Gorakhpur on Saturday that Delhi’s air has become like a gas chamber, making breathing difficult and causing eye irritation, while Gorakhpur’s environment is pure. He added that if you protect the environment, it will protect you. 5- ‘You bought Rafale—will the Make in India lion rust?’ The SP chief said they do not want to discuss Epstein and that social media is problematic. He questioned when the files were prepared and why they surfaced later. He said several countries have created their own social media platforms, so India must stay cautious in a changing world. Calling the files just one issue, he said the government has handed over the entire market to the US and would give it a $500-billion market. “You bought Rafale worth ₹3 lakh crore—will the Make in India lion rust?” he asked. 6- ‘Azam Khan was treated unjustly’ Akhilesh said excessive spending was done for self-promotion. Panchayat polls are being delayed because of large-scale voter-list irregularities. He claimed the government had already prepared village head voter lists before drafts were released. On rising crime, he said it is bound to increase when the Chief Minister is like this. He alleged insult to Ahilyabai Holkar and said the Pal community would remove them from power. He also claimed BJP leaders even stole the one hour given by Nepal’s king. He accused BJP of demolishing 100 temples and said they would face consequences. He added that Azam Khan was treated unjustly and everyone wants him released. Without government and courts, justice is difficult, he said, adding he cannot comment on the High Court. 7- On Owaisi’s brother’s remark: ‘He’ll come riding a bicycle’ When asked about AIMIM chief Asaduddin Owaisi’s brother Akbaruddin Owaisi saying he would come to UP and plant his flag, Akhilesh replied, “He will come riding a bicycle.” Why SP made this move — explained in 3 points 1- Message: SP is the only party concerned about the community Siddiqui has also served as Congress’s provincial president in western UP, where he is believed to have strong influence among Muslim voters. Currently, Congress leader Imran Masood is more active there and often attacks SP. BSP had also been increasing its outreach among Muslims in western UP. SP now hopes to counter this through Siddiqui and send a message that it alone truly represents the community’s concerns. 2- Attempt to blunt MIM’s edge Senior journalist Ejaz Hasan says a narrative is often created that the SP chief speaks less about Muslims because he believes that vote bank will not drift away. With MIM strengthening in Bihar and Maharashtra, SP leaders fear it could dent their core vote bank in UP. By inducting Muslim leaders before elections, Akhilesh aims to signal that Muslim voters remain firmly with SP. This is also seen as an attempt to blunt Owaisi’s party’s influence. 3- Impact from Bundelkhand to western UP Siddiqui has long been known as a major political figure. His joining SP is expected to have an impact from Bundelkhand to western UP, especially in Muslim-dominated areas where MIM is trying to expand. He could be projected as a counterweight there. Why he resigned from Congress — explained Was ignored in Lok Sabha polls There had been dissatisfaction over Siddiqui’s role and influence in Congress, and he was not given importance in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections. With the 2027 assembly polls approaching, he was worried about his future in the party. The rapid rise of Saharanpur MP Imran Masood, considered close to Priyanka Gandhi, also troubled him. Recently, while receiving Rahul Gandhi at Amausi airport, he was reportedly not allowed entry ahead of leaders like Pramod Tiwari and Aradhana Mishra. On 24 January, Siddiqui resigned from Congress. In his letter he wrote that he had joined to fight casteism but could not work on the ground for eight years and felt he was “rusting.” He said he respects Rahul Gandhi, Mallikarjun Kharge and Sonia Gandhi, and always will, but there was no role for him in the party. He added he had joined to fight communalism but could no longer do so. Why he wasn’t attacking Congress — reason now clear Siddiqui had not been aggressive against Congress. Photos of Rahul, Priyanka and Sonia Gandhi, along with BSP founder Kanshi Ram, still hang at his residence. In an interview, he had said he never intended to weaken Congress. Now it is clear why he stayed soft—the SP-Congress alliance continues in UP. National leaders of both parties have indicated it will remain for the 2027 assembly elections as well. He had therefore been cautious not to make remarks that Congress could turn into an issue. Read about Naseemuddin Siddiqui Career began as railway contractor Siddiqui has long been a prominent name in UP politics. Born on 4 June 1959, he came from a non-political family. After leaving an army job due to his mother’s illness, he became active as a railway contractor. Around 1990 he came into contact with Kanshi Ram and began with municipal elections. He joined BSP in 1984 and in 1991 was elected MLA from Banda for the first time, becoming BSP’s first Muslim legislator. Known as ‘Mini CM’ in BSP government He served as minister in all BSP governments. In the 2007–2012 BSP regime he held 18 departments and was called “Mini CM.” He was considered among Mayawati’s closest aides, influential in ticket distribution, finances and organisation. From 2012 to 2017 he was Leader of Opposition. In 2017 Mayawati expelled him from BSP, after which he formed his own party. In 2018 he joined Congress and was projected as a Muslim face. Now, a year before the assembly polls, he has also left Congress. Having resigned on 24 January, his new political home is now set to be SP, where he will take membership with supporters in Akhilesh’s presence on 15 February.

stories.summary: Lucknow News: 14 फरवरी 2026 को लखनऊ में एक बड़ी घटना हुई। बेंगलुरु से लखनऊ आ रही एयर इंडिया एक्सप्रेस की फ्लाइट (IX 2048) में यात्री और क्रू मेंबर के बीच विवाद हो गया। यह विवाद सीट और खाने को लेकर शुरू हुआ। लैंडिंग के बाद मामला पुलिस तक पहुंच गया। यह घटना शनिवार 14 फरवरी को हुई। फ्लाइट बेंगलुरु से लखनऊ जा रही थी। इसका निर्धारित समय सुबह 10:35 बजे लखनऊ पहुंचना था, लेकिन आधे घंटे की देरी से यह 11:05 बजे पहुंची। विमान में यात्री अंकित सहाय अपनी पत्नी शालिनी प्रिया और तीन साल के बेटे के साथ यात्रा कर रहे थे। वे लखनऊ घूमने आए थे। अंकित के साले केजीएमयू में डॉक्टर हैं और परिवार उनके यहां ठहरा हुआ है।

stories.title: Minister Nishad compares Pakistan to street dog:Fans say Pak will be crushed; excitement high over India-Pak match in UP
stories.summary: A T20 World Cup match between India and Pakistan will be played in Colombo, Sri Lanka, today at 7 PM. Ahead of the match between the two countries, the excitement among fans in UP is high. In Lucknow, cricket enthusiasts, dressed in Indian players' jerseys, performed 'Jalabhishek' (offering water) to Lord Shiva. They prayed for India's victory. In Kashi, fans performed a special puja at Scindia Ghat. Young Brahmins (Batuks) also participated. Chants of 'Har Har Mahadev' were raised. Fans held posters with slogans like 'Pakistan will be crushed...'. During the special puja, fans lit lamps on the banks of the Ganges. They wished for India's victory. Amidst patriotic slogans, fans said - Cricket is not just a game, but because it's a match between India and Pakistan, it is also linked to the nation's honor. Previously, a match between India and Pakistan took place in the Asia Cup on September 28, 2025. India had won that match. A special screening of the match will be held at KD Singh Babu Hostel in Lucknow. Meanwhile, live arrangements have also been made for players to watch the match at Guru Gobind Singh Sports College. stories.title: Husband gets wife married to nephew:Man claims she could have killed him like Meerut drum case, if he refused
stories.summary: A woman married her nephew outside a police station, where they exchanged garlands and took seven vows before a sacred fire in Baghpat. The marriage reportedly took place with the consent of the woman’s husband. The husband alleged that his wife used to mix sleeping pills in food to make him and their children sleep, and would then go to meet the nephew. He claimed that if he had not agreed to the marriage, she might have killed him “like the Meerut drum murder case”. He added that he has now severed all ties with his wife and plans to leave with his children to start a new life elsewhere. After the ceremony, the couple did not return home. Family members say they have left for another city. The 28-year-old woman was married 8 years ago and had reportedly been in a relationship with her 22-year-old nephew for the past five years. The incident falls under the Doghat police station area. Family members tried to explain, but they didn't listen Tikri town is 55 kilometers away from the district headquarters. Pankaj, who lives here, was married to Pooja 8 years ago. They have two children. The elder son is 5 years old, and the younger one is 3 years old. Pankaj said that just 3 years after marriage, Pooja started having an affair with Sanjeev, her own nephew, who lived in the neighborhood. Upon learning about this, I tried to make Pooja understand and stopped her from meeting the nephew. On this, Pooja started quarreling. The matter reached the panchayat. Villagers tried hard to explain to Pooja and Sanjeev, but neither listened. There were frequent disputes at home regarding this matter. Husband said - I was under mental stress I started having frequent fights with Pooja. Nephew Sanjeev also started quarreling with me. I was under mental stress due to my wife's illicit relationship. It was also badly affecting the children. She would mix sleeping pills in food to make me and the children sleep, and then go to my nephew. I was afraid that if I tried to stop them both anymore, Pooja would put my children and me in a blue drum. Both families were fed up with their behavior. So we decided to get them married. On Friday evening, we took both of them to the police station. I informed the police about the whole matter. The police counseled both parties and sent them back. But as soon as they came out of the police station, Pankaj got wife, Pooja, married to nephew, Sanjeev. Both of them exchanged garlands in front of Pankaj and family members. 'I have nothing to do with my wife anymore' Pankaj also gave in writing to the police that both are getting married by their own will. Now, they have nothing to do with Pankaj, and he has no complaints. Both loved each other, so I got them married on my own will. Now, there is nothing left for me in this village. Villagers said - Husband himself arranged the marriage According to villager Krishnapal, the woman and her relative youth had been in a love relationship for quite some time. On Saturday, both arrived at the village with their families. There they got married to each other. The woman's husband also gave his consent for this relationship. The children will stay with their father. Station in-charge Suryadeep Singh said - No written complaint has been received in the matter. Information has been received that both exchanged garlands outside the police station, no further information is available.

stories.title: Varanasi’s Noor Fatima builds Rudreshwar Mahadev temple:Performs puja alongside namaz, says, 'shattered after husband’s death, Bholenath supported me'
stories.summary: 'I have been a lawyer in the Varanasi civil court since 1993. When I came to live in this colony with my husband, continuous accidental deaths were happening here. People were troubled. Meanwhile, I started having dreams of large temples. On this, the colony people said that you should visit the Mahamrityunjay Temple or Baba Vishwanath. But I said I am Muslim, why should I go?' The series of deaths continued here. My husband, Murad Ali, was an engineer in BLW. One day, he also left home, had an accident, and died. After that, I remained in depression for some days. Then built this temple. Where, I come to offer water daily. After my husband's death, Lord Shiva has taken care of me.' This is what senior advocate Noor Fatima from Varanasi has to say. Noor Fatima's house is in Ganeshpur Colony, located near BLW. Noor Fatima built a Shiva temple here in 2004. People from the entire colony come here for worship and prayers. Noor Fatima herself comes here daily in the morning and evening to offer water to Lord Shiva. She also offers white garlands, which she had seen in her dream. Noor Fatima is one of the senior advocates of Varanasi. Being a Muslim, why did she build this temple? How much faith does she have in it, and what kind of support does she get from the neighbors? On all these matters, Dainik Bhaskar visited the Rudreshwar Mahadev Temple in Ganeshpur Colony, Varanasi, to closely understand this living example of Noor Fatima and Ganga-Jamuni culture. Read the report... See the pictures of Rudreshwar Mahadev Temple... First, know the truth about building the temple?... Often saw temples in dreams Noor Fatima said - This was around 2002. We had just moved to this colony. The people here are very friendly. After coming here, I often started seeing large Shivalays in my dreams. Wherever I went, I would offer white garlands on the Shivling. When this continued for several months, I informed the people in my neighborhood about this. They initially said it's nothing to worry about. But these dreams didn't stop. Go have darshan of Baba Vishwanath or Mahamrityunjay Noor Fatima said - After this, when I discussed it, people said come with us to the Mahamrityunjay temple. That's where we go for darshan because there are huge crowds at Baba Vishwanath's court. To this, I angrily said why should I go to the temple when I'm Muslim. I pray five times a day, so why should I go for darshan at the temple? Concerns grew as sudden deaths increased Noor Fatima said - During this time, sudden deaths increased in our colony. Old people, young people, and children started dying suddenly. No one knew when someone would die. Every evening after sunset, people would gather in one place and discuss this, and people would start crying, remembering their loved ones. Days passed like this, and I continued to have dreams. Husband's Sudden Death Too Noor said - On the ill-fated morning of April 10, 2004, my husband, Murad Ali, left home for some work, and 20 minutes later, I received a phone call that he had met with an accident. When we reached there, he had been taken to the hospital. Where he died. After his passing, I went into depression because I only had two daughters. Even in this depression, I kept having dreams of the temple. I can say that Baba Bholenath supported us after my husband's death. Built temple after discussing with colony residents Noor Fatima said - After this, she discussed this matter with the colony residents and started the temple construction work by laying the first brick herself on November 27, 2004. This temple was completed in three months. After the temple was built, I now come here daily for darshan. The entire neighborhood comes here to worship. Since then, I have been coming here every morning and evening to offer water to Baba Bholenath. Daily darshan along with Namaz and Ramadan fasts Noor said - I haven't left Islam. I offer all five daily prayers and keep all fasts during Ramadan. But my time for Shiva worship doesn't change. I come to the temple daily morning and evening to offer water and a garland. Now know what the neighborhood people said about Advocate Noor Fatima and the temple?... Noor worships just like us Suman Rai, a resident of Ganeshpur Colony, said - This is Rudreshwar Mahadev temple, which was built by Advocate Noor Fatima. She comes daily for darshan and worship just like us, Hindu brothers. It never felt like Noor Fatima is different from us or is Muslim. In our neighborhood, this temple and Noor Fatima are giving the message that we are all one. This division is only political. We are all one and will always remain one. Leaders want us to keep fighting among ourselves Rajendra Singh also lives in Ganeshpur Colony. He said that he has been living here for the past 20 years. People had thought of building a Shiva temple here, but couldn't. Noor Fatima had a dream about the Shiva temple. She told us, and then we collected donations to build this temple, in which Noor's contribution was the highest. Speaking about the country's atmosphere, he said - This is all about politics, and they want us to keep fighting among ourselves all the time for their own selfish interests. Now, know who Advocate Noor Fatima is? Married to Engineer Murad at BLW Advocate Noor Fatima is from Faizabad. In 1986, she got married to Murad Ali, an engineer working at BLW (which was DLW at that time) in Varanasi. After marriage, she soon moved to Varanasi. While staying here, she obtained her law degree from Lucknow University. Civil Lawyer since 1993 Noor Fatima said - I started going to the Varanasi court in 1993. I fought many civil cases, and today I am a successful advocate. Before retirement, my husband bought a piece of land near Ganeshpur Colony after BLW's Kandwa Gate. We were supposed to return to Lucknow, but at that time, the Bhuj earthquake happened, so I suggested that we build a house here and stay here. After that, we built a house here. They have two daughters. One is in America, and one is an advocate in the Allahabad High Court.

stories.title: 'You are Dalit, I am OBC’:Girlfriend refuses marriage, heartbroken man dies by suicide after final meeting; mother files FIR against her
stories.summary: “My son was deeply in love with Saumya. He used to say he was the hero of Aashiqui 2. She was his entire world. But Saumya loved his money, not him. As long as he was earning well, everything was fine. The moment he lost his job, she began distancing herself. She refused to marry him, saying, ‘You are Dalit and I am OBC.’ My son could not bear the heartbreak and ended his life.” These are the words of Kiran Pakhare, mother of Tushar Pakhare, who died by suicide in Jhansi on February 6. On the day of the incident, Tushar had called Saumya for one final meeting. After she left, he was later found hanging. His mother was not at home at the time. Following his last rites, Kiran Pakhare lodged an FIR against Saumya Sahu, accusing her of abetment to suicide and invoking provisions of the SC/ST Act. Met at coaching, friendship turned into 7-year relationship Tushar Pakhare (24) lived in the Badagaon Gate outer area of Jhansi. His mother, Kiran Pakhare, said Tushar was the younger of her two sons. His elder brother lives in Delhi with his family, while his sister Pooja is married and also resides in Jhansi. Tushar lost his father, Dinesh, when he was just seven years old. “I raised him as both mother and father,” Kiran said. At the time, the family lived near Orchha Gate, where a girl named Saumya Sahu was their neighbour. In 2019, Tushar joined coaching classes at Rajiv Sir’s institute in Ganj. Saumya also attended the same coaching centre. Their friendship began there and gradually developed into a romantic relationship. According to the family, the two remained in a relationship for nearly seven years. Initially, Saumya had agreed to marry Tushar, and both families were aware of their relationship. The two had also spent time together on several occasions. 'Saumya used to say - You are SC, I am OBC' Mother Kiran said - After studies, Tushar started working in Bhojla Mandi. He used to earn 30 thousand rupees every month and spent all the money on Saumya. As long as he was earning well, Saumya was happy. As soon as he lost his job, she started having objections. Initially she had no problem with caste, but later she refused to marry. She said - you are Khatik, from SC caste and I am Sahu, from OBC caste. Therefore cannot marry. After this she started creating distance, which Tushar could not bear. 'Son used to say - Mom, I am the hero of Aashiqui-2' Mother said - After losing his Mandi job, Tushar started working at Shivam Color Lab, where the salary was very low. After finding this out, Saumya started troubling him. Tushar loved her very much. Whenever there was talk of Saumya, he would say - Mom, I am the hero of Aashiqui-2. I tried to explain to him, but he said he cannot live without Saumya. Two days before dying, he was looking at horoscopes and saying that he would become a big person, go abroad and do business. I did not know that he would leave this world so soon. Mother said - If I had known, I wouldn't have left Mother said - My son Tushar was murdered. Soumya killed him. She says she left, but she didn't go anywhere. She's the one who killed my son. My son wasn't so weak that he would commit suicide. After his death, neither did she call nor come home. On February 6, I went to my daughter's house. My son was alone at home. If I had known, I wouldn't have left my child alone. I wouldn't have even let Soumya wander around, knowing that she was coming to kill my child. He murdered my son. How could she take him down from the noose alone? I cannot understand how in 15 minutes she met him, hanged him and took him down from the noose. I want to know now how my son died. What did she do to my son? Friend arranged their last meeting Tushar's friend Rishi Tiwari said - There had been a dispute between them for some time. Saumya had broken up and clearly refused to live together. After this, communication between them was happening only through me. Tushar had asked me to arrange one last meeting. When I talked to Saumya, she agreed. On February 6, I went to pick up Saumya and dropped her at Tushar's house. After this, I left from there. When Saumya went to get her purse, Tushar was found hanging According to friend Rishi Tiwari, later Saumya told that she had refused to live with Tushar and was going home. After a while, she realized that she had forgotten her purse at Tushar's house. When she went to get the purse, Tushar was found hanging there. Saumya brought Tushar down from the noose and then called me. As soon as I got the information, I reached the spot with my friends. After this, Tushar was taken to the medical college by ambulance, where doctors declared him dead.

stories.title: Skull garlands and fire bursts amaze devotees:Artists dressed as spirits dazzle onlookers at Shiv Baraat
stories.summary: On the occasion of Mahashivratri in Varanasi, more than one million devotees have gathered in Kashi. Baba Vishwanath was adorned like a groom, and the Mangala Aarti was performed at 2:15 am, followed by a ritual Panchamrit abhishek.. The deity was decorated with peacock feathers and a rudraksha garland, after which the temple gates were opened for devotees at the Kashi Vishwanath Dham complex. Officials showered flower petals on the devotees as they entered, while queues stretched across nearby lanes. A 5-km-long queue of devotees has formed, with each person getting barely two seconds for darshan. The temple will remain open for continuous darshan for 45 hours. VIP and VVIP protocols have been cancelled today. Arrangements have been streamlined so that devotees reach the sanctum within about 25 minutes of joining the queue. Foreign devotees from 10 countries, including the United States, have also arrived. Visitors from California said they felt blessed after the darshan and described the city as beautiful. Mariyana from Russia said they came to understand Lord Shiva. Most hotels, lodges, and dharamshalas in the city are fully booked. ATS commandos have been deployed for security, and surveillance is being carried out through drones. Meanwhile, in Prayagraj, the final holy dip of the Magh Mela is underway on Mahashivratri, with heavy crowds at the ghats since morning. The administration estimates that 1.5 to 2 million devotees may take the final dip. Devotees are also thronging Shiva temples across the state, including in Lucknow and Gorakhpur.

stories.title: Cricketer commits suicide after shooting girlfriend in Noida:Caste opposition and family pressure culminate in tragedy
stories.summary: On Valentine's Day in Noida, a lover killed his girlfriend in her car, then committed suicide by shooting himself. During investigation, police found a 1-year-old note in Sumit's handwriting. Sumit wrote- I have no relationship with Rekha. If I harass her in any way, action should be taken against me. This was the time when Sumit and Rekha's families found out about their affair. Rekha's family was not ready for marriage. Two reasons emerged for this. First- Cricketer Sumit's career was ruined after a road accident. Second- he was from the Valmiki community. Rekha's family was Kayasth. They did not want to give their upper-caste daughter to a boy from the backward caste. After 1 year of struggle, Sumit chose the path of death. Before the murder and suicide on February 13, Sumit picked up Rekha from her office, after which they did not return home. Both families had filed missing persons reports at Sector-58 police station in Noida. On February 14, their bodies were found in a white Altroz car in Sector-39. According to the doctor who conducted the post-mortem, bullet wounds were found in the heads of Sumit and Rekha. Read the report... Affair began from school friendship Sumit and Rekha first met at the public school in Trilokpuri. They studied together in 10th and 12th grade. They belong to the same campus, and conversations began, which turned into a deep relationship. Both families were open-minded, so no one objected to them visiting each other's homes for academic preparation. Initially, they would only visit each other's homes to study. But later, they started participating in family wedding events as well. The relationship was so close that family members started considering it routine. Not just studies, Sumit and Rekha shared similar interests too. Sumit was a good right-handed batsman. He used to play in events across UP, Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan, and Gujarat. Rekha also liked cricket. They would often talk on the phone. Rekha got a job, Sumit started water supply business After 12th, Rekha completed B.Com graduation. Then she started working in Sector-62. Meanwhile, Sumit set up a water plant with help from his father. Sumit's father, Rajiv, works as a health inspector in the Delhi MCD (Delhi Municipal Corporation). Sumit began supplying water to different societies. Along with this, he continued playing cricket. However, he earned good money. Meanwhile, Sumit started making life plans with Rekha. Both wanted to get married. Sumit's brother said - My brother bought a ₹1 crore flat in Noida. He wanted to gift it to Rekha. He would give Rekha branded gifts frequently. He would pick up and drop Rekha from her office in Sector-62 by car every day. Everything was going well. Cricket career ruined after accident The first U-turn in this love story came in 2019. Sumit had a road accident in Noida's Sector-107. Sumit was badly injured in this. The doctor said that you cannot go into sports. During this time, Rekha stayed with him from the hospital to home. It took him 6 to 7 months to recover. This was the period when both families came to know about their love. The biggest obstacle in this affair was their community. Because Sumit was from the Valmiki community, while Rekha was Kayasth. The tension between the upper and lower castes had now come between their relationship. Sumit's family members were ready for this marriage, but Rekha's family did not want to give their daughter to a lower caste. They slowly started explaining to Rekha that if you marry Sumit, how will we face society? Sumit's brother, Sachin, alleges - After this, Rekha's family members forbade Sumit from coming to their house. If Sumit was even seen around the house, they would threaten him. This went on for a long time, but there was never a fight between the two families. Cousin brother threatened - If you trouble my sister, I will file an FIR According to the family, in early 2025, Sumit was caught near the house by Rekha's family members. The cousin brother threatened that stay away from Rekha. Otherwise, they would file a molestation case with the police. Some chats from that time have also been received by Dainik Bhaskar. In which Sumit is apologizing. He is saying that I made a mistake, so I won't meet. Please don't file a complaint. According to the family, after this incident, Rekha also stopped answering Sumit's calls. Sumit had given in writing to her family- I have no relationship with Rekha. If I harass or trouble her in any way, action should be taken against me. I will be personally responsible for this. Marriage stuck due to caste issues, Sumit became troubled However, even after all this happened, they continued to meet. Sumit remained troubled because he couldn't marry Rekha just because of caste issues. Meanwhile, Rekha also couldn't bear to see her friend troubled. On February 13th at 3 PM, Sumit left home in his car. At 3:39 PM, he messaged Rekha's mobile. He wrote - I am going to die. Rekha messaged him back, then he reached Rekha's office in Noida. Rekha came out of the office and sat in his car. According to family members, Rekha used to return home by 6 PM every evening, but that day she didn't reach home till night. Everyone was worried; they checked with the office. They found out that she had left with someone in a car. The family suspected Sumit. They contacted Sumit's house and learned that he was also not at his home. After this, both families went to the police. A missing persons report was filed at Noida Sector-58 police station. Sumit's phone had been switched off since 6 PM, while Rekha's mobile was on until the morning of February 14th, but she was not receiving anyone's calls. Bodies of both found in car at 1:30 On February 14 at 1:30 PM, the Sector-39 police station found a white Altroz car. The car was locked from inside, so the police broke the glass to open the door. Inside, the bodies of Sumit and Rekha were found. Sumit had a pistol in his hand. Looking at the circumstances, it appeared that Sumit shot Rekha and then committed suicide. Both had bullet wounds in their heads. Two shells were lying beside them. After conducting the post-mortem of Sumit and Rekha, the police handed over the bodies to their families. Sumit's family performed his last rites in Delhi. Meanwhile, Rekha's funeral was conducted in Noida Sector 94.

stories.title: Story of mother-in-law entangled in love relationships:Woman seeks son-in-law's arrest; know reality behind marriage with brother-in-law
stories.summary: Anita Devi from Aligarh has 3 children, 2 sons and 1 daughter. Anita arranged her daughter's marriage. The engagement was also done. She gifted a phone to the son-in-law after the engagement. The son-in-law used that phone to talk to his would-be wife. Gradually, conversations started between Anita and the son-in-law. To such an extent that the son-in-law now talked more with his mother-in-law than with his fiancée. When 10 days remained before the wedding, both left their homes. They ran away to live together. Son-in-law Rahul and mother-in-law Anita lived together for about 10 months. Then they had a fight between themselves. Anita left the son-in-law and went to her brother-in-law Devendra's place. Rahul reached the police station. Made several serious allegations. On the other hand, Jitendra, the husband whom Anita had left, also got married. When Anita went home, he didn't talk to her. The daughter whose marriage was to take place is still the same today. There are many questions in this whole matter. Husband Jitendra has accusations. Wife's defense and then allegations regarding the son-in-law. A story has also emerged about brother-in-law Devendra. Today in Sunday Big Story, we learn about this entire matter from one side... Got daughter engaged, used to talk with son-in-law for 15-20 hours Madrak police station is located about 13 kilometres from the Aligarh district headquarters and includes Manoharpur Kayasth village. Farmer Jitendra lived there with his wife Anita and their three children. The couple had been married for around 20 years, while Jitendra worked in Bengaluru. Last year, the family began searching for a match for their daughter Shivani. Through relatives, they were introduced to Rahul, a resident of Nagla Machhariya village in the Dadau police station area. At the time, Rahul worked as a supervisor in a private company in Rudrapur, Uttarakhand. Both families approved of the match, and the engagement was finalised in January, with Rahul’s brother-in-law, Yogesh, playing a key role in arranging the alliance. After the engagement, Anita gifted Rahul a mobile phone. He began speaking with his fiancée Shivani, and the two slowly got to know each other, though Shivani’s shy nature meant their conversations remained limited. For this reason, when Rahul would call, Anita would pick up the phone. Gradually, this pattern increased. Rahul and Anita started talking to each other on the phone. When Anita's husband Jitendra would call from Bangalore, the number would show as busy. When asked, it would turn out she was talking to her son-in-law. Jitendra would also think that since he's the son-in-law, it's okay. Both ran away 10 days before the wedding and kept running Shivani and Rahul's wedding was scheduled for April 16, 2025. All preparations were underway. Wedding cards were being distributed. However, on the other side, Anita and Rahul grew closer. On April 6, Rahul left his house, saying he was going to buy a sherwani and never returned. Similarly, Anita also left alone, saying she was going shopping, and went with Rahul. When both didn't return at night, the search began. A missing persons report was filed. Later, it was discovered that both had run away together. Anita's husband, Jitendra, complained at the police station that his wife fled with three and a half lakh rupees kept for the wedding and jewellery worth 5 lakhs. Police filed a report and began the search. Meanwhile, Rahul and Anita kept running from one place to another. First, they went to Delhi, then to Bihar. From there, they went all the way to Nepal. For 10 days, they kept moving from one place to another. During these 10 days, both travelled 2826 kilometres. Tired and exhausted, they returned to Aligarh. They surrendered themselves to the police at Dado police station. Children started crying together, husband was ready to take them At Dado police station, police also called the family members of Anita and Rahul. Jitendra came with both children. The 9-year-old son started crying while clinging to Anita. Police started counselling both of them. Asked them to go back to their respective homes. However, both were not ready to separate. Jitendra had also agreed that if Anita agreed to come home, he would take her along. But Anita was not ready. She said that Rahul understands her feelings. Respects her. She spent 9 days with him and got to know him well. She can spend her entire life happily with him. Anita said about Jitendra - He would only beat me up. He would beat me up even for ₹100-200. On the other hand, Rahul's father Omvir and others were trying to explain to him. But, he was also not ready to understand. Omvir even said that Anita had tied a black thread around my son's neck and controlled him. My son is not listening because of black magic. One more thing was discovered here. Even 2 months before the marriage was fixed, Rahul had eloped with a woman from the village. On February 6, Anita was freed from Rahul's captivity. She returned to Aligarh from Sitamarhi. She reached her brother-in-law Devendra's house in Bhawanipur. On the other hand, Rahul went to the Dadri police station and filed a complaint. Rahul alleged that over the past two to three months, Anita’s behaviour changed as she began speaking frequently with her brother-in-law, Devendra and quarrelling over minor issues. He claimed she demanded ₹1,500 to send to her sister, leading to a dispute, after which he transferred the money. In his complaint, Rahul also alleged that Anita left with ₹2 lakh in cash and jewellery and accused her of plotting to poison him and flee. Expressing regret, Rahul said eloping with Anita was a mistake and that he should have married her daughter instead. He claimed Anita has a pattern of running away and will not stay anywhere for long. Anita, however, rejected his claims, calling her decision to go with Rahul the biggest mistake of her life. She accused him of daily beatings, confinement and exploitation, and demanded legal action against him. Police called both to the station, but no resolution was reached, and Anita’s family has refused to accept her back. After the police station, Anita went to her home in Manoharpur. After going there, she found out that her husband Jitendra had married again last month. He married a woman from near Atrauli. No one at home talked to Anita. They didn't even let her stay at home. Troubled by this, Anita went back to her brother-in-law Devendra's house in Bhawanipur. Regarding the allegation of running away with brother-in-law Devendra, she says this is all lies. Rahul is defaming her. Her brother-in-law has his own complete family. He is a simple person who drives vehicles. 'The talk of affair with me is wrong' Dainik Bhaskar spoke to Anita's brother-in-law, Devendra, about this matter. Devendra was previously a driver at Trans India. He had an accident recently, after which he is currently at home. Regarding the affair with Anita, he says - This is a very wrong rumour being spread. I have no such involvement. I have my own family. Rahul is spreading all this; he should understand himself. Rahul is a bad person. His marriage was fixed with the daughter, but he developed a relationship with the mother-in-law herself. Regarding bringing Anita with them, he says - Initially, when she came to Aligarh, she first went to the police station. After that, she went to her village, Manoharpur. No one talked to her there. A panchayat meeting was held in front of the SSP. Then the police told me that Anita's family members are not keeping her, so you take her with you. We brought her. She stayed here for 1 day, and on February 13, she left my house. Don't we know where she is now? No truth in allegations of taking cash and jewellery In this entire matter, complaints reached the police several times. When the son-in-law and mother-in-law fled, Anita's husband alleged that she took ₹3 lakh and a half and jewellery. At that time, Anita had said that she left home with only ₹200. Now, Anita is accusing Rahul of taking ₹2 lakh, 500 grams of silver and other jewellery. Here, the question also arose that when Anita left home with only ₹200, then where did the jewellery and money come from? On the other hand, Rahul alleged that Anita took ₹2 lakh in cash and jewellery from the house. These allegations also don't seem to have any merit. Because whatever Rahul had remained at his house. The business he was currently doing didn't generate much income, according to him. It was just enough to run the household. Police are trying to resolve this matter through the panchayat rather than the law. However, they don't seem to be successful here either. Anita's first husband has gotten married. Because of this, Anita's return has become difficult. However, divorce hasn't happened between them. The girl Shivani, whose marriage started all this, still hasn't gotten engaged.

stories.title: Shankaracharya raises concern over safety threats:Says, 'How can I ask security from those plotting my murder'
stories.summary: "How can we seek protection from those who want to kill us? We have already presented our side before the court. Those who are criminals themselves are making allegations against us. Ashutosh is in contact with cow slaughterers.” These statements were made by Shankaracharya Swami Avimukteshwaranand. Ashutosh Brahmachari, a disciple of Jagadguru Rambhadracharya and Shakumbhari Peethadhishwar, has filed a case in court against the Shankaracharya, accusing him of sexually exploiting two disciples. Following the hearing, the court has reserved its order. On February 21, it will decide whether an FIR should be registered against the Shankaracharya or the case should be dismissed. During this period, Dainik Bhaskar spoke with Shankaracharya Swami Avimukteshwaranand in Varanasi regarding the allegations and the ongoing legal proceedings. Here is what he had to say. Question: What do you have to say about the sexual harassment allegations? Shankaracharya: Look, the person making these allegations against us has a criminal background himself. Reports have previously appeared in the media stating that he was in contact with individuals involved in cattle smuggling and cow slaughter. He was also accused of being caught offering bribes to get trucks cleared. Being accused by such a person speaks for itself. We have already said that the campaign being run against us is a result of our stance on cow protection and our call to stop cow slaughter. Today, those whose interests are connected to cow slaughter are the ones actively targeting us. Question: Do you believe this is a conspiracy against you? Shankaracharya: We believe that whatever attacks are taking place are driven by ideology. When you speak about protecting the cow, it is natural that those involved in cow slaughter will oppose you. This is not surprising. Question: Will you demand additional security from the government? Shankaracharya: We have never asked anyone for security, and we do not intend to do so now. It is the responsibility of the state to ensure the safety of its citizens. If the government feels that security should be increased, that is its decision. We will not approach anyone to request protection. We have faith in God. Our scriptures say that one who is under the Lord’s protection cannot be harmed by anyone. Our security comes from our Sanatan Dharma community and our faith in God. How can we ask those who want to kill us to protect us? Question: Has political interference in religious matters increased? Shankaracharya: There is a need to reflect on the relationship between religion and politics. It appears that certain forces want to bring religious institutions under their influence. In Hindu tradition, the roles of religious leaders and rulers have remained separate. If political power begins positioning itself at the centre of religious leadership as well, it disrupts the natural balance. Society must reflect seriously on this. Question: How do you view the 2027 Assembly elections? Shankaracharya: We do not work with any particular election or year in mind. Our clear view is that whoever becomes Chief Minister should be law-abiding and treat the people like their own children. A person driven by ego, revenge, or oppression cannot be suitable to govern a state. Uttar Pradesh is a fertile land with no shortage of capable and hardworking individuals. They should be given opportunities. Question: Are you questioning the Chief Minister’s leadership? Shankaracharya: We speak about principles, not individuals. In a democracy, no position belongs permanently to anyone. There are many capable people in society, and leadership is ultimately judged by the public. Question: Had you previously praised Keshav Maurya? Shankaracharya: At that time, his statement appeared balanced and thoughtful, so we welcomed it. It was not an expression of political support, but a response based on the situation. After that, there was no further significant discussion on the matter. What happened during the Mauni Amavasya bath... On January 18, during the Magh Mela on Mauni Amavasya, Avimukteshwaranand was going for a bath in a palanquin. The police stopped Shankaracharya Swami Avimukteshwaranand's palanquin. The police asked him to walk to Sangam. The disciples of Shankaracharya did not agree and started moving forward with the palanquin. On this, a scuffle broke out between the disciples and the police. Police had detained several disciples. Police had also beaten a sadhu at the police post. This angered Shankaracharya and he insisted on getting the disciples released. Officers tried to reason with him, folded their hands, but he did not agree. After this, police detained several more supporters of Shankaracharya. Shankaracharya's palanquin was dragged 1 km away from Sangam. During this, the canopy of the palanquin also broke. Shankaracharya could not even take a bath. Shankaracharya remained on protest outside his camp until January 28. Then returned to Varanasi. Shankaracharya had said- High-ranking officers were beating our saints. At first we were returning, but now we will bathe and not go anywhere. They cannot stop us. They must have orders from above to harass us. This is happening at the government's behest because they are angry with us. When there was a stampede in Mahakumbh, I had held them responsible. Now they must be telling officers to take revenge.
