stories.title: Heat rises early across Uttar Pradesh:Summer 2026 could have record temperatures, say experts
stories.summary: Half of February has not yet passed, yet summer is already beginning to make its presence felt in Uttar Pradesh. While mornings and evenings still carry a slight chill, the afternoon sun has grown noticeably sharper. During the recent winter season, cold conditions affected much of Uttar Pradesh and North India. Now, there are indications that just as winter was intense, summer this year could also set records. Early signs of rising temperatures are already visible. According to the India Meteorological Department (IMD), 2025 was the country’s eighth warmest year. Before that, 2024 was recorded as the warmest year on record. In this context, projections emerging for 2026 are raising concern. This leads to key questions: how severe will the heat be this time? Could 2026 surpass the record set in 2024? And how cold was the recent winter? Winter conditions this year Mahesh Palawat, Vice-President (Meteorology and Climate Change) at Noida-based Skymet Weather, explained that Uttar Pradesh experienced milder winter conditions compared with the previous two years. In December and January, both average maximum and minimum temperatures remained above normal. Typically, winter maximum temperatures in North India range between 20°C and 22°C, while minimum temperatures range between 10°C and 15°C. According to Palawat, both parameters were higher than average this season, and extreme cold was not observed. He attributed the milder winter to the absence of La Niña conditions. Mohammed Danish, a scientist at the Lucknow Meteorological Centre, also confirmed that this winter was less severe than last year. What is La Niña? La Niña is a global climate pattern in which ocean waters become cooler than usual. When this cooler water evaporates, cloud formation increases, influencing rainfall patterns. In India, whether rainfall will be deficient or abundant, and whether temperatures will trend colder or hotter, is significantly influenced by La Niña. Before winter 2025 began, the IMD had estimated that La Niña might develop, potentially intensifying cold conditions in North India. However, La Niña did not materialise in the Pacific Ocean, and therefore, a sharp increase in cold was not observed. At the beginning of the season, the United States weather agency NOAA had estimated a 60 per cent probability of La Niña becoming active during winter, with possible effects lasting until March. This scenario did not occur. Reduced western disturbances and rainfall deficit Meteorologist Mohammed Danish noted that the activity of Western Disturbances over Uttar Pradesh was also limited during the winter season. As a result, rainfall during the cold months remained below normal. Extended periods of cloud cover and fog typically intensify cold conditions, but such patterns were largely absent this year. In most districts, sunshine prevailed during the day. According to IMD data, Uttar Pradesh recorded a 36 per cent rainfall deficit between 1 January and 11 February. February trends and short-term outlook Professor Manoj Kumar Srivastava, a meteorologist from Banaras Hindu University’s Geophysics Department, stated that the region is currently experiencing spring conditions. Over the next two to three weeks, significant changes are unlikely. Mornings and nights will remain slightly cool, while afternoons will feel warmer. Mahesh Palawat indicated that light drizzle may occur around 18 February in districts including Hathras, Mathura, Prayagraj, Varanasi, Banda, Lalitpur and Jhansi. Experts agree that winter is now in its final phase and temperatures will gradually increase. Record temperatures in early 2025 For the first time since temperature records began in 1901, the average minimum temperature in February 2025 remained above 15°C. January 2025 was also recorded as the third-warmest January since 1901. The World Meteorological Organisation (WMO) confirmed that 2024 was the warmest year on record globally, with Earth’s temperature rising by 1.55°C that year. Outlook for Summer 2026 According to Professor Srivastava, weather conditions in Uttar Pradesh will change markedly from the first week of March, marking the onset of summer. Both daytime and night-time temperatures are expected to rise rapidly. By the last week of March, maximum temperatures in many districts could reach 35°C to 38°C. In April, temperatures are likely to hover around 40°C. He further indicated that maximum temperatures could climb to 42°C to 45°C in several districts. Relief from heat may be limited even at night, with humidity persisting. However, he cautioned that precise predictions depend largely on the El Niño situation. If El Niño persists or strengthens, summer conditions could intensify further, increasing the number and duration of heatwave days. Climate change and urban heat Dhruvsen Singh, Head of the Department of Earth Sciences at Lucknow University, highlighted structural factors contributing to rising heat. Rapid deforestation, disappearance of natural water bodies, expanding urban concrete infrastructure and increased vehicular traffic are collectively driving temperatures upward. Urban areas may face heightened severity due to the Urban Heat Island effect. Experts assess that 2026 could see above-normal heat in Uttar Pradesh, with more frequent and prolonged heatwaves. National and global projections IMD projects that maximum and minimum temperatures across India will remain above normal from March to May. In March, both are expected to exceed normal levels nationwide, and heatwave days are likely to be higher than usual. Only Northeast India and certain peninsular states, including Maharashtra, Karnataka, Kerala, Odisha and Andhra Pradesh, are expected to experience normal heatwave frequency. El Niño, like La Niña, originates in the Pacific Ocean. When El Niño occurs, India’s monsoon weakens, often leading to drought in several states. Meteorologists currently express concern that if El Niño develops, severe heat could follow. Impact on Agriculture Professor P.K. Singh of BHU’s Agriculture Department warned that March could prove challenging for farmers. Rapid temperature increases during the grain-filling stage of wheat could reduce yield. Excessive heat prevents proper grain development. Hot winds and moisture deficiency may also damage mustard, gram and peas. Rising temperatures dry soils quickly, increasing irrigation costs and crop stress. Global heat concerns A report by Environment and Climate Data UK suggests that 2026 could rank among the four hottest years globally. Rising greenhouse gas concentrations and natural factors such as El Niño continue to elevate global temperatures. Projections indicate that average global temperatures in 2026 may be 1.4°C to 1.5°C above pre-industrial levels. Such warming could undermine Paris Agreement goals, increasing the likelihood of extreme heat, droughts, floods and abrupt weather events, directly affecting health, agriculture and daily life.

stories.title: 'Suicide’ was actually hit-and-run: Dubai Police use AI-powered digital twin to crack case
stories.summary: Dubai Police are now using advanced Digital Twin technology for crime scene investigations. This system creates precise virtual replicas of crime scenes. It has already helped solve cases like a bridge-fall incident, initially thought to be suicide, which was reclassified as a hit-and-run. Another case involving a structural collapse was also solved using this technology.

stories.title: Sabarimala case: 9-judge SC bench to hear pleas on discrimination against women at religious places
stories.summary: A nine-judge Supreme Court bench will hear pleas concerning women's religious entry rights, including the Sabarimala Temple case, starting April 7, 2026. The court will examine the intersection of essential religious practices, equality, and constitutional morality across various faiths. This hearing follows a 2018 ruling that permitted women of all ages into the Sabarimala temple.

stories.title: 'Will not take any step in secrecy': Former Assam Congress chief Bhupen Borah resigns ahead of assembly elections
Why school bus commutes in UAE are raising health, learning concerns
stories.summary: The UAE has introduced new limits for school bus journeys, capping travel at 45 minutes for young children and 60 minutes for older students. This move addresses concerns about long commutes impacting children's health, sleep and academic focus. Global research highlights physical discomfort, air pollution exposure and mental stress as key issues linked to extended travel times.

stories.title: First-of-its-kind mission: US airlifts next-gen nuclear reactor on C-17 aircraft — watch how it was done
stories.summary: The United States successfully airlifted a miniature nuclear reactor for the first time using a C-17 Globemaster III aircraft as part of Operation Windlord. This marks a significant step in rapidly deployable nuclear energy systems, aiming to enhance energy security for military bases and strengthen national security.

stories.title: First solar eclipse of 2026: Can UAE residents see the ‘Ring of Fire’ on February 17?
stories.summary: The first solar eclipse of 2026, an annular event known as the 'Ring of Fire,' will occur on February 17. While invisible from the UAE due to its remote path over Antarctica and the Sun being below the horizon, live streams will be available. A total solar eclipse will be visible in parts of Europe in August 2026.

stories.title: Over 300 prisons running at twice their capacity
Saudi Arabia announces revised school timings for Ramadan across regions
stories.summary: Saudi Arabian education authorities have adjusted school schedules for Ramadan, with most morning classes starting between 9 a.m. and 10 a.m. Continuing and adult education programs will shift to evening hours. These changes aim to support fasting students and staff while maintaining academic standards and administrative efficiency.

stories.title: 'Why is it not paying tax?': Priyank Kharge levels ‘money laundering racket’ charge against RSS
stories.summary: Karnataka Minister Priyank Kharge has accused the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh of engaging in money laundering and questioned its sources of income. He demanded that the RSS, an unregistered organization, be held accountable and pay taxes like other citizens and entities under the law and Constitution.

stories.title: 'Pick up the baton': Mani Shankar Aiyar's pitch for Pinarayi Vijayan sparks row; Congress draws line
Can you use WhatsApp Web voice, video calls in UAE after recent updates?
stories.summary: WhatsApp Web is rolling out voice and video calling worldwide. Users can now make calls directly from their browser. However, these features are blocked in the UAE. Local laws restrict Internet calling services. Residents can use approved apps like BOTIM and Zoom for voice and video calls. Messaging features on WhatsApp Web remain unaffected in the UAE.

stories.title: UAE, Elon Musk's Starlink to bring digital classrooms in 100 remote villages globally
stories.summary: The UAE has partnered with SpaceX's Starlink to bring digital education to remote students globally. This initiative, launched at the World Government Summit 2026, uses satellite internet to overcome infrastructure barriers, enabling access to online learning platforms and resources. The first phase targets 100 underserved locations, aiming to bridge the digital divide and empower learners worldwide.

stories.title: What is Singapore-India-Gulf subsea cable system that UAE's du is investing in for high data connectivity?
stories.summary: UAE telecom provider du has partnered to invest in the Singapore-India-Gulf (SING) submarine cable system, a new undersea fiber-optic network linking the Middle East with South and Southeast Asia. This strategic move reinforces the UAE's position as a regional data hub, enhancing connectivity for AI, cloud services, and global digital growth.

stories.title: Gujarat, Maharashtra, UP lead rooftop solar figures
stories.summary: Gujarat, Maharashtra, and Uttar Pradesh are leading in rooftop solar installations. Over 23 lakh systems have been installed nationwide under the PM Surya Ghar scheme. The government aims to install one crore systems by 2027. Monthly installations have significantly increased since the scheme's launch. Financing and awareness remain key areas for improvement.

stories.title: India adds record 52.5 GW in first 10 months of FY26
Election Commission suspends 7 West Bengal officials over ‘serious misconduct’ linked to SIR
stories.summary: The Election Commission of India has suspended seven officials in West Bengal for alleged serious misconduct and dereliction of duty. These Assistant Electoral Registration Officers, posted across Murshidabad, South 24 Parganas, West Medinipur, and Jalpaiguri districts, face immediate disciplinary proceedings. The Commission has directed the Chief Secretary to initiate action without delay and provide an update.

stories.title: Aiyar wants Left return in Kerala, Cong says it’s a personal view
Op Sindoor showed Shiva's Rudra resolve, says Rajnath Singh
Rahul Gandhi demands PM Modi reply to 5 'simple queries' on India-US trade deal
Lok Sabha may take up opposition's notice against Speaker Om Birla on March 9

Defence spend, upgrade in line with current realities: PM Modi
India's global AI challenge: Over 4k entries cut to 70 finalists
AI models & campus labs: India's tech push at summit
'Delhi declaration' may be adopted at AI summit in Delhi
stories.summary: India has launched its first comprehensive AI governance guidelines, opting for a flexible, principle-based approach to foster innovation while managing risks. These seven 'sutras' emphasize trust, people-first development, fairness, and accountability. The framework relies on existing laws and proposes new institutions to oversee AI, aiming to position India as a leader in responsible AI development.

stories.title: Europe and America lose millions of Christians, Africa now largest region with 697 million believers
stories.summary: Christianity remains the world’s largest religion at 2.3 billion people, but its global share is shrinking as religious switching accelerates, especially in Western countries. While Europe and North America see steady decline, sub-Saharan Africa now anchors the faith’s growth. The data reveals not collapse, but a geographic and cultural shift reshaping Christianity’s global center of gravity.

Epstein ranch twist: MAGA candidate Don Huffines named as mystery buyer of Jeffrey Epstein's New Mexico home
MacKenzie Scott donates $26 billion in seven years, surpassing Elon Musk and Jeff Bezos in lifetime giving
Presidents Day 2026: What will be closed — banks, government offices and more
stories.summary: Presidents Day, observed on the third Monday of February, honored all U.S. presidents, originally established to celebrate George Washington's birthday. In 2026, it fell on February 16, leading to closures of government offices, banks, and postal services. The holiday's official name remains Washington's Birthday, though it evolved to recognize all commanders-in-chief.

EAM S Jaishankar greets Serbia on Statehood Day during visit to Munich Security Conference
stories.summary: The External Affairs Minister had earlier met Serbian Foreign Affairs Minister Marko Djuric on the sidelines of the conference on Saturday. In a post on X, Jaishankar said, "Greetings to FM @markodjuric, the government and people of Serbia on their Statehood Day. Appreciate our long-standing partnership."

stories.title: CPRG to host multiple events at India AI Impact Summit 2026 in New Delhi; focus on AI in education, employability, and data governance
stories.summary: The Center of Policy Research and Governance (CPRG) will host the India AI Impact Summit 2026 from February 16-20 in New Delhi. The event will feature discussions on AI's impact on education, employability, data governance, and institutional transformation, with sessions held at various venues. Senior ministers, policymakers, and industry leaders are expected to participate.

stories.title: Rajasthan: Delhi CM Rekha Gupta offers prayers at Shrinathji Temple on Mahashivratri
stories.summary: Rekha Gupta expressed, "Today, on the occasion of Mahashivratri, I feel incredibly fortunate to have had the opportunity to offer prayers to Lord Shrinathji. I am filled with a profound sense of peace and joy. "

stories.title: Iran-US indirect talks: Tehran’s top diplomat travels to Geneva for second round
stories.summary: Iran's foreign minister heads to Geneva for crucial indirect nuclear talks with the US, mediated by Oman. This follows earlier discussions that stalled due to regional conflict. Tehran seeks economic benefits, including sanctions relief, while Washington demands a halt to uranium enrichment. Tensions remain high with potential military action looming.

stories.title: Imran Khan undergoes eye examination at Adiala Jail: PTI calls process 'malicious', questions exclusion of family and personal doctors

stories.summary: Viral social media posts and a YouTube video claimed Erika Kirk was arrested while fleeing to Israel over grooming allegations amplified by Candace Owens. Public court records and US law enforcement databases show no arrest, no investigation, and no charges against her. The screenshots behind the claim remain unverified, and no official source confirms wrongdoing.

stories.title: 'Am not a politician anymore and can't be': Barack Obama reveals reason why 'Michelle would divorce' him
stories.summary: Barack Obama humorously stated that a return to elected office would likely end his marriage, crediting Michelle Obama's influence. He emphasized their post-presidency focus on empowering the next generation through the Obama Foundation, rather than seeking personal power. Their new Chicago center will embody this vision, fostering emerging leaders.

stories.summary: Former President Barack Obama stated that aliens are real but he has not encountered them, dismissing claims of their presence at Area 51. He also revealed that upon entering office, he inquired about extraterrestrial life and was informed no such studies were underway. Obama acknowledged that unexplained aerial phenomena are taken seriously by officials.

Marco Rubio says, US ‘not disputing’ European report blaming Russia for Navalny poisoning
stories.summary: US secretary of state Marco Rubio stated Washington is not disputing a report by five European nations concluding Alexei Navalny was fatally poisoned. The report identified a rare toxin from a dart frog, with Russia identified as the prime suspect. Navalny's widow declared his murder a "science-proven fact" after his death in a Russian penal colony.

stories.title: From Wall Street to Hollywood: Casey Wasserman latest hit in Epstein files fallout — read full list
stories.summary: Casey Wasserman, a prominent Hollywood talent agent, is selling his business following the release of Epstein files that exposed communications with Ghislaine Maxwell. Wasserman apologized for past personal mistakes impacting clients and partners. Several other individuals, including Kathy Ruemmler and Brad Karp, have also faced consequences due to their connections with Epstein revealed in the documents.

stories.title: What will be India's 3 reform priorities for next decade? Here's what PM Modi said

stories.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi emphasized the private sector's crucial role in India's economic future, urging bold investments in innovation and capacity. He highlighted his government's commitment to reforms and decisive governance, while also stressing the need for the private sector to share productivity gains with workers and invest in R&D and quality.

stories.title: 'Hallyu' from Seoul: How South Korea's K-wave swept India - and its darker side
stories.summary: South Korea's 'Korean Wave' has transformed from a niche phenomenon to a mainstream cultural force in India and across the globe, driven by K-pop, K-dramas, and lifestyle trends. This soft power surge, fueled by digital access and strategic state policy, offers a model for global influence, impacting consumption and aspirations across the nation.

stories.title: ‘A lecture from a country ranked 58th?’: Kaja Kallas fires back at Marco Rubio on free speech
stories.summary: Estonian official Kaja Kallas sharply responded to US Secretary of State Marco Rubio's remarks on free speech. Kallas highlighted Estonia's high ranking in a freedom of speech index, contrasting it with the US's lower position, suggesting a lecture from the US was 'interesting'.

stories.summary: Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju announced that the Lok Sabha will debate and vote on a no-confidence motion against the Speaker on March 9. This follows a submission by 118 Congress MPs alleging partisan conduct. Historically, such motions against Speakers are rare, with past instances including those against GV Mavalankar, Sardar Hukum Singh, and Balram Jakhar.

stories.summary: Jammu and Kashmir security agencies have frozen over 8,000 mule accounts in three years, identifying them as crucial for global scam networks and potential funding of anti-national activities. These accounts facilitate the conversion of stolen money into untraceable cryptocurrency, with authorities urging banks and law enforcement to curb their rise and identify "mulers" who manage them.

stories.title: “Back to her maiden name”: Internet erupts over Erika Kirk’s “missing” posts as Candace Owens dispute intensifies
stories.summary: Online speculation erupted after a viral screenshot suggested Erika Kirk deleted Facebook posts months after Charlie Kirk’s death. The image showed a page under her maiden name displaying “no posts available,” prompting debate amid her ongoing feud with Candace Owens. However, no verified reports confirm deletion, and differences in accounts, privacy settings, or inactive pages may explain the confusion.

stories.title: “Regret the love….”: Gigi Alayah’s cryptic post fuels drama after Kai Cenat finally addresses breakup
stories.summary: Kai Cenat addressed rumors surrounding his December 2025 breakup with Gabrielle “Gigi” Alayah, apologizing for his silence and urging fans to respect both sides. Hours later, Alayah reposted a quote about love and having no regrets, sparking speculation online. While she offered no explanation, fans viewed the message as a graceful response and a sign she has moved forward.

stories.title: Isha Mahashivratri 2026 to be livestreamed with sign language interpretation
stories.summary: Isha Yoga Center's Mahashivratri, themed 'Ganga', will be a global livestream event on February 15-16, featuring sign language interpretation and broadcasts in 23 languages. Defence Minister Rajnath Singh will be the chief guest. The program includes guided meditations by Sadhguru, musical performances, and for the first time, Sadhguru will perform the Yogeshwara Linga Maha Abhishekam.

stories.title: Big boost for Assam: CM Himanta Biswa Sarma says Rs 55,000 crore projects cleared in last one year
Owaisi’s big charge on Centre over SIR, says BJP using EC to ‘snatch citizenship’
stories.summary: Asaduddin Owaisi alleged the BJP-led government is trying to "snatch citizenship rights" through the special intensive revision of electoral rolls, claiming it will be conducted in Telangana and Maharashtra. He also condemned the alleged harassment of a Muslim bun vendor by YouTubers, demanding action against them.

stories.title: “It’s a lavender marriage”: Laura Loomer claims Candace Owens wanted to have children with Charlie Kirk instead of her husband
stories.summary: Candace Owens is facing renewed online speculation after Laura Loomer claimed she once wanted to marry Charlie Kirk and have children with him. The allegation, shared without evidence, quickly spread on social media and drew attention to Owens’ marriage to George Farmer. The debate comes as Owens continues discussing Kirk’s death, keeping public interest in her personal life high.

stories.title: Soap opera over soap: Why Karnataka politics is in a ‘lather’ over iconic Mysuru brand
stories.summary: At the heart of the row is Karnataka Soaps and Detergents Limited (KSDL), the government-owned company that manufactures Mysuru Sandal Soap. Founded during the reign of Nalwadi Krishnaraja Wadiyar, the brand is not merely a commercial product. For many Kannadigas, it is an aromatic symbol of heritage. Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) MP K Sudhakar accused the Congress-led Karnataka government of displaying what he called an “anti-Kannada mindset”.

stories.title: Countdown to Ramadan: Qatar calls on public for Moon sighting on February 17
stories.summary: Qatar's Ministry of Endowments has called on the public to sight the crescent moon on the evening of February 17 to determine the start of Ramadan. Muslims are urged to report any sightings to the ministry's headquarters. The Crescent Sighting Committee will convene after Maghreb prayer to review testimonies and officially announce the beginning of the holy month.

stories.title: Dubai’s Ramadan 2026 plans revealed: 30 days of daily fireworks, drone shows, cultural events
stories.summary: Dubai is set to host a spectacular Ramadan 2026, commencing February 19th or 20th, with a vibrant calendar blending spiritual observance and city-wide festivities. Expect dazzling drone light shows and fireworks illuminating the night sky, alongside cultural installations and community gatherings. These events aim to unite residents and visitors in a celebration of light, art and shared experiences.

stories.title: India deputes Om Birla, Vikram Misri to Dhaka for Bangladesh PM-elect Tarique Rahman's swearing-in
stories.summary: Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla will represent India at the swearing-in of Bangladesh's PM-elect Tarique Rahman, following the BNP's landslide victory. Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri will accompany Birla. This event marks a significant diplomatic shift for Dhaka, especially after former PM Sheikh Hasina's ouster and subsequent exile in India. The new BNP government's stance will be closely observed.

stories.title: 'Betraying farmers' vs 'spreading lies': Rahul Gandhi, Amit Shah clash over India–US deal
stories.summary: Rahul Gandhi accused the Modi government of betraying farmers through the India-US trade deal, raising concerns about GM maize imports and potential pressure on Indian crops. Union Home Minister Amit Shah refuted these claims, calling them lies and asserting that farmers' interests are protected in trade agreements with the US, EU, and UK.

stories.title: Tamil Nadu polls: Congress seeks ‘due respect’ ahead of seat-sharing talks with DMK
‘Focus on devotional aspect of life’: Sri Sri Ravi Shankar urges devotees to embrace meditation on Mahashivratri
stories.summary: Spiritual leader Sri Sri Ravi Shankar urged deep inner reflection and devotion this Mahashivratri, emphasizing meditation and chanting to elevate spiritual practice. Prime Minister Modi and defence minister Rajnath Singh extended greetings, praying for well-being and prosperity. The festival celebrates the divine union of Lord Shiva and Goddess Parvati, observed with reverence across India.

stories.title: Ramadan 2026 iftar hiking trend: Why Muslims are opting to trek and break fast in UAE's mountains, deserts
stories.summary: In the UAE, a unique Ramadan tradition is gaining traction: iftar hikes. Residents are embracing organised treks in the Hajar Mountains and deserts, breaking their fast together at sunset. This trend blends spiritual reflection, community bonding and outdoor wellness, offering a serene alternative to city celebrations and fostering a deeper connection with the holy month's spirit.

stories.title: 14.9% of the world, 126 million added: What Pew's religious survey reveals about the Hindu rate of growth between 2010 and 2020
stories.summary: According to the Pew Research Center’s global demographic study “How the Global Religious Landscape Changed From 2010 to 2020,” the actual Hindu rate of growth today turns out to be strikingly literal. The world’s Hindu population has been expanding almost exactly in line with the growth of humanity itself. Neither surging dramatically nor shrinking in relative terms, Hinduism’s demographic story is one of stability in a century defined by rapid religious change.

Kedarnath shrine to reopen on April 22; dates for Badrinath, Gangotri, Yamunotri Dham also announced - check
stories.summary: Kedarnath Temple will welcome devotees from April 22, concluding its winter hiatus. The auspicious reopening date was fixed on Mahashivratri at the shrine's winter seat. This marks the commencement of the Char Dham Yatra, with Badrinath opening on April 23, and Gangotri and Yamunotri on April 19. Thousands are expected to participate in the pilgrimage.

Massive crackdown: Saudi Arabia arrests over 21,000 for residency and labour law violations in one week
stories.summary: Saudi Arabia's crackdown on residency, labour, and border security violations yielded over 21,000 infractions in a week. Authorities arrested thousands attempting illegal entry and exit, including those aiding them. Severe penalties, including hefty fines and imprisonment, await offenders and facilitators. The ministry urges public reporting of violations.

stories.title: Ramadan 2026 working hours in the UAE: Revised timings from Feb 19
stories.summary: The Philippine Embassy in Abu Dhabi and Consulate General in Dubai have announced revised, shorter working hours for Ramadan 2026, from February 19th. These adjustments aim to accommodate fasting practices and ensure efficient service delivery for the large Filipino community in the UAE. Residents are urged to book appointments early and rely on official advisories for updated information.

stories.title: Pakistan linked to the ‘death squad’ kidnappings haunting Balochistan streets
stories.summary: Recent disappearances in Balochistan, including at least seven individuals in Panjgur and Karachi, are linked to Pakistan's security apparatus. Residents reported raids and detentions, with families of those taken, like Zulfiqar and Zakir Noor, receiving no information, raising fears of secret confinement.

stories.title: 3 jailed in Dubai Marina for hijacking mobile signals: How the SMS banking scam worked
stories.summary: Dubai authorities have sentenced three men for a sophisticated mobile signal hijacking scam in Dubai Marina. The criminals used jamming equipment to create fake networks, tricking residents into connecting and then stealing financial information via malicious links. This high-tech fraud bypasses traditional security, highlighting growing cybercrime risks in the UAE.

stories.title: Saudi Arabia introduces new Arabic policy to expand use in schools, courts and tech sector
stories.summary: Saudi Arabia has launched a historic National Policy for the Arabic Language, aiming to modernize its use in business, science, and global influence. The policy, with eight core principles, seeks to reinforce Arabic's status as a pillar of national identity and cultural security, promoting its vibrant presence across all sectors of life.

stories.title: 'White-collar' terror probe: Doctors formed 'Ansar Interim' to carry out attacks
stories.summary: A new terror outfit, 'Ansar Interim,' formed by radicalised doctors, has been exposed by J&K Police. The group, allegedly linked to Al-Qaeda, planned subversive activities, including IED attacks. Investigations revealed procurement of explosive materials and attempts to recruit members, with a key operative planning a VBIED blast.

stories.title: Saudi Premium Residency for exceptional talent: Salary requirements and eligibility for foreign professionals explained
stories.summary: Saudi Arabia's Exceptional Talent Premium Residency now welcomes more entities, but strict salary requirements remain. Researchers need SR14,000 monthly, while scientific/healthcare pros require SR35,000. Top executives must earn SR80,000. This selective program targets experienced professionals and leaders, offering five-year renewable residency with family benefits and property ownership.

stories.title: 'If the opposition doesn't allow the House to function, we will go for the guillotine': Rijiju
stories.summary: Union Minister Kiren Rijiju announced that the no-confidence motion against Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla will be debated and voted on March 9. The second part of the Budget session, starting the same day, is expected to be "interesting" with crucial legislation. Rijiju warned that continued opposition protests could be detrimental to them and suggested potential cracks in opposition unity.

stories.title: Maharashtra Congress chief likens Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj with Tipu Sultan; booked for hurting sentiments
stories.summary: Maharashtra Congress chief Harshwardhan Sapkal has courted controversy by comparing Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj with Tipu Sultan. His remarks have led to a police case against him. Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis condemned the comparison. Meanwhile, Congress leader Sachin Sawant accused the BJP of double standards and a polarization agenda, citing past BJP endorsements of Tipu Sultan.

stories.title: Oman issues urgent warning after man swims with killer whale
stories.summary: Oman's Environment Authority has issued a stern warning against diving near orcas following a viral video of a man swimming close to the powerful marine predators. The advisory emphasises the unpredictable nature and immense strength of these wild animals, stressing that such close encounters pose serious risks to both human lives and wildlife wellbeing.

stories.title: 'Time to end Islamic republic': Exiled prince Reza Pahlavi urges Donald Trump to help Iranian people
stories.summary: Reza Pahlavi, son of Iran's last shah, has appealed to US President Donald Trump. He called for an end to the Islamic republic, stating it is the demand of the Iranian people. Pahlavi asked Trump to help Iranians, referencing the President's earlier remarks about change in Iran. Trump has increased military pressure on the Islamic republic.

stories.title: Saudi Arabia: Madinah education department announces revised school timings for Ramadan
stories.summary: Madinah schools are set to commence their academic day at 9:30 a.m. starting the first day of Ramadan 1447 AH. Education authorities have confirmed these revised timings for all boys' and girls' schools across the region. This adjustment aims to harmonize learning with the spiritual and daily routines of the holy month, ensuring academic continuity while supporting students and staff.

stories.title: Saudi Arabia warns of SR50,000 fine for unreported visa overstays, jail and deportation risk
stories.summary: Saudi Arabia is cracking down on visit visa overstays, holding sponsors accountable. Failure to report expired visas can lead to hefty fines up to SR50,000, imprisonment, or deportation for non-Saudi residents. Authorities also warned against aiding violators, emphasizing strict enforcement and confidential reporting of any breaches.

stories.title: UAE job boom 2026: 2,700+ jobs to open in Ras Al Khaimah as mega resort nears launch
stories.summary: Ras Al Khaimah's Wynn Al Marjan Island is transitioning from construction to a major employment hub, with 2,700 jobs to be filled by its early 2027 opening. Recruitment is now focusing on mid-management and specialized technical roles, offering significant opportunities across hospitality, operations, and corporate functions for UAE professionals.

stories.title: Renting to buying your first house in UAE 2026: 5 real estate trends home owners should focus on
stories.summary: UAE's property market is seeing a surge in first-time homebuyers in 2026, driven by government support and a shift towards long-term value. Buyers now prioritise build quality, practical design and community infrastructure over speculation. Affordability and tech-driven mortgage solutions are making ownership more accessible, fostering a generation committed to homeownership as a lifestyle choice.

stories.title: UAE issues 25 new AI guidelines for schools, prohibits use for under-13 students
stories.summary: The UAE has unveiled strict AI guidelines for schools, banning generative AI for students under 13 and mandating disclosure for older learners. The policy emphasizes critical thinking over AI reliance, prohibits culturally insensitive or harmful content, and fortifies data privacy. AI will be a mandatory subject, aiming to equip students with ethical understanding and technological mastery.

stories.title: NEET-PG cut-off: Single-digit scores land PG seats in top med colleges
stories.summary: NEET-PG qualifying standards were drastically lowered, resulting in postgraduate medical seats in government colleges being filled with extremely low scores. Candidates secured spots in high-risk clinical specialties and premier institutions with scores as low as single digits, raising significant concerns within the medical community.

stories.title: In 'clear message', Malaysia, India slam cross-border terror
stories.summary: Malaysia joined India in condemning cross-border terrorism, signaling a stronger alignment on the issue. Prime Minister Modi highlighted clear messages against terror with no double standards or compromise. The bilateral meeting saw numerous agreements signed, spanning defense, security, and economic cooperation, including semiconductors and social security for Indian workers.

stories.title: Left politics a 'retrograde ideology': PM Modi
stories.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi lauded BJP MP C Sadanandan Master's courage after he displayed prosthetic legs in Rajya Sabha, highlighting an attack by alleged CPM supporters. Modi criticized "retrograde ideology" for shrinking political ground, while praising Master's presence in Parliament. He also noted Kerala's fatigue with traditional alliances and appreciation for the BJP's vision.

stories.title: Isro study shows safe patch near Moon’s Mons Mouton for Chandrayaan-4 landing
stories.summary: ISRO scientists have identified a promising one-square-kilometre landing zone near Mons Mouton in the Moon's south polar region for the Chandrayaan-4 mission. Detailed terrain analysis using high-resolution images has shortlisted the MM-4 area as the safest option for India's first lunar sample return. This site offers gentle slopes, adequate sunlight, and minimal hazards, crucial for the mission's success.

stories.title: 99% of jobs could vanish by 2027 – only 5 types may survive, warns AI expert
stories.summary: AI researcher Dr. Roman Yampolskiy warns that artificial general intelligence could automate nearly all jobs by 2027, driving unprecedented unemployment. Unlike past revolutions, few human roles would remain, limited to oversight, AI intermediaries, counseling, or niche human-made crafts. He predicts society may reach a technological singularity by 2045, where AI progress outpaces human comprehension, fundamentally challenging the relevance of human labor.

stories.title: ‘America’s elections are rigged, stolen’: Trump renews claims, warns US must fix system or lose country
stories.summary: Former President Donald Trump is once again asserting that American elections are rigged, demanding sweeping reforms like mandatory photo ID and proof of citizenship to restore trust. He proposes limiting mail-in voting, framing these as crucial for the nation's survival.

stories.title: From remembrance to ashes: Memorial for 41 victims of Swiss nightclub fire goes up in flames
Rahul Gandhi's message to Gen Z: 'Be flexible and persevere'
stories.summary: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi advised Gen Z to be flexible and persevere, emphasizing that life is not linear. He shared insights from an interaction with NRI students, addressing their anxieties about confidence, judgment, and self-expression. Gandhi highlighted the importance of staying true to oneself amidst societal pressures and labels.

stories.title: PM Modi sets May deadline to prioritise quality improvement of highways
stories.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi has set a May deadline for the road transport ministry to prioritize highway quality improvement and develop robust SOPs. This directive follows numerous complaints about poor road conditions, especially post-monsoon. The PM also called for action against underperforming contractors and a study into potential collusion affecting land acquisition delays.

stories.title: India, Canada step up security cooperation
stories.summary: National Security Advisor Ajit Doval's visit to Canada has yielded a "shared workplan" for bilateral cooperation on national security and law enforcement. Both nations agreed to establish liaison officers to enhance communication and information sharing on critical issues like drug trafficking and organized crime. This move aims to rebuild trust and pave the way for future high-level engagements.

stories.title: Trade deal a threat to India's interests: CPM
stories.summary: CPM and CPI(ML) Liberation have strongly criticized the Indo-US trade deal, alleging the BJP government has made significant concessions detrimental to India's economy, agriculture, and national sovereignty. Both parties demand the deal's details be made public and presented to Parliament, urging the government to halt any agreement harmful to Indian workers and farmers.

stories.title: ‘Did everything right, still failed’: Indian student plans to leave US after job hunt stalls
stories.summary: A 27-year-old Indian man, after completing a Master's degree in the US, is returning to India due to an inability to secure employment. Despite aggressively applying for jobs daily, he faced rejections citing visa status and sponsorship needs, a situation exacerbated by new H-1B petition fees.

stories.title: Electronics output up 6-fold, exports 8-fold in 11 yrs: Govt
stories.summary: India's electronics manufacturing has surged six-fold in production and eight-fold in exports over 11 years, making it the world's second-largest mobile phone maker. Driven by the production-linked incentive scheme, mobile production alone saw a more than 100-fold export increase, transforming India into a net exporter.

stories.title: StableRonaldo sparks controversy after pointing gun on IRL stream
stories.summary: Popular streamer StableRonaldo sparked outrage after a clip showed him pointing a handgun at another car in Los Angeles during a live stream. He claimed he felt followed. Viewers debated if the weapon was real, but displaying any firearm, even a replica, in public can lead to serious legal trouble in California, highlighting the dangers of IRL streaming.

stories.title: Trade deal will give new wings to farmers' dreams: Shivraj Singh Chouhan
stories.summary: Union Agriculture Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan stated that the India-US interim trade deal will empower farmers, with key agricultural products like major grains, fruits, and dairy remaining secure from US imports. He asserted that the agreement protects farmers' interests and will boost Indian exports, particularly in textiles.

stories.title: Nayara's future unsure: India may bargain with US for Russian crude
stories.summary: US President Trump's threat of a 25% "penalty" on Indian crude imports casts a shadow over the Nayara refinery, majority-owned by Russia's Rosneft. This situation fuels speculation about a change in ownership, as prospective buyers may be deterred by US sanctions.

stories.title: In a first for India, a desi aerospace firm gains in-orbit snooping capability, takes images of ISS
stories.summary: India's space sector has achieved a significant milestone as Azista Space successfully imaged the International Space Station from its own satellite. This groundbreaking "space watch" capability, demonstrated by the ABA First Runner satellite, marks a first for any Indian company. The feat enhances India's space situational awareness, crucial for protecting national assets in orbit.

stories.title: Mizkif-linked Twitch account receives temporary suspension
stories.summary: Popular streamer Mizkif's secondary Twitch account received a 24-hour suspension for promoting a competitor in the stream title. Twitch enforces strict rules against using its platform's discovery features to direct viewers elsewhere, even for minor violations on non-main accounts. The brief suspension served as a reminder of Twitch's policies on platform promotion.

stories.title: Did ancient Egypt record biblical giants? A 3,300-year-old text raises new questions
stories.summary: A 3,300-year-old Egyptian papyrus held by the British Museum has reignited debate over whether biblical references to giants reflect historical encounters or myth. The Anastasi I manuscript describes unusually tall Shosu people, drawing interest from faith-based researchers while historians urge caution, noting the text’s likely satirical nature and the lack of archaeological evidence supporting the existence of ancient giants.

stories.title: Streamer Kyedae confirms breakup with TenZ, ending six-year relationship
stories.summary: Popular Twitch streamer Kyedae Shymko has announced her breakup with VALORANT personality TenZ after six years together. The couple, who started dating at 17, mutually decided to part ways due to growing apart and a need for individual growth, not a specific conflict. Their separation, hinted at by social media changes, brings closure to fans.

stories.title: Colder than Antarctica? What caused New York’s life-threatening deep freeze
stories.summary: New York City experienced temperatures colder than parts of Antarctica on Sunday, with wind chills reaching 14 degrees below zero. This extreme cold, driven by Arctic air, prompted rare warnings for millions. The prolonged deep freeze marks the most extreme in at least a decade for many Northeast locations.

stories.title: Young J&K MLA draws praise from across the aisle for House speech
stories.summary: A young BJP legislator, Devyani Singh Rana, earned cross-party praise for her focused budget speech in the J&K Assembly. She highlighted critical issues like electricity shortages, climate vulnerabilities, and under-spending in education and disaster management, urging for stronger measures. Her pragmatic approach to budgetary concerns resonated with members from all parties.

stories.title: Highway builders seek PM’s intervention on PPP project timelines, arbitration curbs
stories.summary: Highway builders are urging Prime Minister Modi to revisit tight construction deadlines for major PPP projects, citing execution challenges and the risk of prolonged court battles due to restricted arbitration. The National Highways Builders Federation warns that current dispute resolution changes could hinder project completion and encourage litigation over actual construction, impacting the PPP highway program's goals.

stories.title: 'Reject this’: Tej Pratap Yadav rubbishes child rumours, says no link with woman named in past Facebook post
India, Malaysia sign 11 MoUs during Modi's visit
India, Canada to forge 'shared work plan' to bolster security cooperation
stories.summary: In a groundbreaking collaboration, India and Canada are setting new standards for national security and law enforcement by introducing a cooperative work plan and appointing liaison officers. This strategic alliance is designed to combat shared threats such as drug trafficking and organized crime, highlighting a pivotal moment in repairing diplomatic ties.

stories.title: Two Indian American men indicted for allegedly using 3,000 stolen identities to defraud online gambling sites of $3 million
stories.summary: Two Indian American men from Glastonbury face federal charges for allegedly using thousands of stolen identities to defraud online gambling platforms, including FanDuel, of approximately $3 million. Amitoj Kapoor and Siddharth Lillaney are accused of exploiting new user incentives with illicitly obtained personal data, leading to charges of fraud, identity theft, and money laundering.

stories.title: Nobel Peace Prize winner Narges Mohammadi sentenced to fresh jail term in Iran
stories.summary: Nobel laureate Narges Mohammadi has received over seven additional years in prison, alongside a two-year travel ban and internal exile, according to her lawyer. The Iranian activist, already incarcerated, is reportedly on a hunger strike. This latest sentence follows her persistent campaigning against the regime's human rights abuses, including the death penalty and mandatory dress codes.

stories.title: ‘India-Japan friendship to reach greater heights’: PM Modi congratulates Sanae Takaichi on poll win
A stream of hope flows in Bundelkhand through 'Har Ghar Nal'
stories.summary: Bundelkhand's long struggle with water scarcity has ended as tap water now reaches homes, a dream realized for millions. Women no longer trek miles, and villages once defined by drought now boast flowing water. This transformation, driven by the Jal Jeevan Mission, brings hope and a better future to the region.

stories.title: Queen Elizabeth's response to Prince Andrew's Epstein links revealed: 'Full support from mum'
stories.summary: Freshly unveiled documents related to Epstein shed light on Queen Elizabeth's delicate perspective regarding Prince Andrew's connection to the financier. Though her spokesperson emphasized her 'complete support' for Andrew, the Queen reportedly expressed privately that his ongoing interactions with Epstein were 'ill-advised.' This revelation surfaced against the backdrop of ongoing examinations into images featuring Andrew alongside Epstein and Virginia Giuffre.

stories.title: Thailand elections: Conservative PM Anutin Charnvirakul claims victory
‘She nearly died’: 18-month-old girl was returned to ICE custody, denied medication despite life-threatening illness, lawsuit says
stories.summary: An 18-month-old girl, Amalia, was hospitalized with a life-threatening respiratory illness while detained by US immigration authorities. She was returned to custody and denied medication after her release from the hospital, amidst a measles outbreak at the Dilley, Texas facility. Her parents, also detained, sued for their release.

stories.title: Australia moves to ban pro-Palestinian slogan under law carrying up to 2 years in jail
Japan snap elections: PM Sanae Takaichi’s LDP secures majority in lower house
stories.summary: Japan's ruling LDP, led by PM Sanae Takaichi, is poised for a significant win in snap elections, exit polls suggest. This victory could empower Takaichi to advance her conservative agenda, including increased defense spending. However, voter concerns about inflation and economic stability persist, alongside heightened regional tensions with China.

stories.title: “His third eye…”: Candace Owens claims Charlie Kirk believed he was psychic and a time traveller
stories.summary: Candace Owens claims Charlie Kirk spoke privately about having psychic abilities, including a “third eye,” astral projection, and unusual childhood experiences. She also alleged he believed he might die young and referenced a CIA program called “Project Looking Glass.” The unverified remarks have sparked backlash, with critics questioning her claims and their impact on Kirk’s legacy.
